BaseIdentity.title: BaseIdentity
BaseIdentity.description:
The spec1 identity-core projection document for one Spec: exactly what
gets hashed to produce its spec_id, serialised once and echoed back
verbatim -- never re-derived by a second, parallel implementation.

Every Spec carries one, on `Spec.definition.identity` (see
`SpecDefinition`). A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts a prior Spec's own
`definition.identity` byte-for-byte as its edited `identity`. Directional
entities live directly in `identity.entities.origin` and
`identity.entities.destination`. StatVar members are graph state, derived from the
identity, and no member here.

The document is hashed whole. `"spec_"` plus the first 32 hex digits of
the SHA-256 of its RFC 8785 serialisation, with null members omitted, is
the Spec's spec_id.

max_candidates.description: the maximum number of candidates applied

A later part that folds into an earlier part's spec carries binding_folded. A part posted with separate: true never folds and keeps its own part, so two separate parts can carry one spec_id by request. Parts sharing a spec_id can differ in assumptions, so a client never dedupes parts by spec_id

CandidateSet.title: CandidateSet
CandidateSet.description:
A set of 2..N competing Specs, presented in the order named by ``ordering``.

``ordering="intent_rank"``: the order the status rule offers the readings in. A first
answer always uses it. The elected reading comes first, then its rivals in menu order,
each stating why it is offered (``ResolvedSpec.basis``). Where the elected reading holds
no data and several siblings differing from it only on the measurement qualifier do,
those siblings are the set, in menu order, without it. Where a place named without a
direction holds data under both, the elected reading under each direction is offered.

``ordering="broadest_first"``: a posted candidates entry that names it
(``ResubmitCandidatesEntry``) keeps its posted order and states this ordering back. No
first answer uses it.

Each candidate carries its own heading and byline inside its own
``resolved.rendered_sentence``/``resolved.sentence_plan``. There is no separate parallel sentence array, and a
candidate's Spec is a returned Spec like any other. The part's own
sentence opens with how many readings there are and states, for each
shown candidate, the source and span that set it apart.

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. Two parts marked separate that resolve to one reading carry the same spec_id and stay two parts. False, the default, is omitted

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order, and a candidates part's then closes with its assumptions clause. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

entity_refs.title: Entity Refs
entity_refs.description: the binding of each entity of `restatement`, one per restatement.entities row, in row order, so a client can tell which node a text such as 'G7' bound. A response field kept off `restatement`, which posts back unchanged. The binding is the one the answer reads: for a candidates part, the elected reading's; for a part folded into an earlier part's spec, its own. [] when `restatement` is null or names no entity

operations.title: Operations

departures.title: Departures

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: every value the engine filled that the request did not ask for, in clause order. Declared defaults come first, in the order of the Spec's trace.slot_filters, then open roles, then the place scope. A declared default is a slot the request left open that its code system's or shape's declared default fixed, named by the bound code's full label. An open role is a flow role no request word asked for, read across every entity on it with data. It is either a role the role scope default filled (resolved.scope on that axis), whatever its member count, served as one series per member where the shape declares the role, or a role the heading states with no entity of its own ('from 164 providers', 'owed to all creditors'), served as the total over its members. A role the identity binds in entities or lists in open_roles, that one of the part's operations runs over ('top 5 donors'), or that the request's words asked every member of ('all donors'), is asked. The place scope is a request that named no place, read across every place with data. Every door fills assumptions. A definite part reads them from its Spec, a candidates part carries the items every list in CandidatesPart.reading_assumptions holds alike, text included, and no_data and unsupported parts carry []. A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts every slot bound, so its part states the items of the entry's assumptions echo that still hold (see ResubmitIdentityEntry.assumptions), and a candidates entry reads each reading with its candidate's echo (see ResubmitCandidate.assumptions). The sentence that carries this part closes with them as one segment='assumption' clause ('Assumed: official development assistance; every provider.'), after its departures. [] when the answer fills nothing

reading_assumptions.title: Reading Assumptions
reading_assumptions.description: each shown reading's own assumptions, keyed by its Spec's spec_id (candidates.specs[].spec_id). Each list is the one a definite part answering that Spec for this part's request carries, read with the part's operations and the axes the request's words asked every member of. The part's own assumptions are the items every list here holds alike, text included, so an open role one reading reads, or an item two readings word differently ('every provider' against 'every creditor'), is stated here alone. A client that picks a reading posts its identity as a dataset_resubmit identity entry and echoes reading_assumptions[spec_id] as the entry's assumptions, so the picked answer states what that reading assumed. A client that edits the set echoes each reading's entry as its candidate's assumptions. [] for a reading that assumes nothing

composition_write_token.description: the cpw_ token that grants creating components into the composition this create started with composition_id "new", sent back as the x-dfo-write-token header. Present only on that create.

CreateReplyResponse.title: CreateReplyResponse
CreateReplyResponse.description:
`POST /api/presentation/components`'s 201 body. It carries
`WriteReplyResponse`'s fields plus this door's own `affordance` line
naming the freshly minted component's revise and read routes.

graph_generation.title: Graph Generation
graph_generation.description: the graph generation token: the graph service's Cloud Run revisions last read, joined with +; null while unknown

origin_catalogue.title: Origin Catalogue
origin_catalogue.description: build id of the origin catalogue this request is bound to

coverage_index.title: Coverage Index
coverage_index.description: build id of the series coverage index; null when none is loaded

code_index.title: Code Index
code_index.description: content hash of the packaged code index export

DataBuilds.title: GraphDataBuilds
DataBuilds.description: The data builds this process serves, each null where it is unknown or absent.

description.title: Description
description.description: its sole Provenance's description, as `details.description`; null when it has several

license_type.title: License Type
license_type.description: licence label every Provenance agrees on, as `license.type`; null when they disagree or one has none

update_cadence.title: Update Cadence
update_cadence.description: release cadence label every Provenance agrees on, as `license.update_cadence`; null when they disagree or one has none

years_covered.title: Years Covered
years_covered.description: `YYYY` or `YYYY-YYYY` span of its Provenances' observation dates, as `scope_and_units.years_covered`; null when either end is unknown

source_url.title: Source Url
source_url.description: the publication's page, as `details.source_url`: the Dataset's url, else its sole Provenance's

DatasetEntry.title: DatasetEntry
DatasetEntry.description:
A Dataset and the admitted provenances that belong to it. A provenance with
no Dataset forms its own entry, keyed by the provenance, so `ref` and `label`
are the provenance's and `provenances` holds that one provenance.

The card facts (`description`, `license_type`, `update_cadence`,
`years_covered`, `source_url`) equal the same members of
`GET /api/graph/documentation/{ref}` for the graph the loaded catalogue
build read. They are null on UN System Data Commons entries.

label.title: Label
label.description: the node's name; for a Provenance, its parent Dataset's name where it has one. Null, and named in gaps, when the graph gives none

types.title: Types
types.description: the node's typeOf values, as the graph holds them

description.title: Description
description.description: the node's prose in the graph; null when it has none

links.title: Links
links.description: each list relation the node has, mapped to its route; empty when none

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: the member path of every value this door cannot know

built_from.title: Built From
built_from.description: the build of each table the response read

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: discriminator for dataset-level re-resolution across every part

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: one entry per response part, in response part order; a single-entry request whose entry is an identity re-resolves exactly that one part

raw_query.title: Raw Query
raw_query.description: original query text, for echo only; does not affect resolution

DatasetResubmitInput.title: DatasetResubmitInput
DatasetResubmitInput.description:
Re-resolve every part of a multi-variable result in one request, so an
edit to one part cannot leave the other parts' composed sentence or fold
stale (see `envelope.make_response` / `conjoin.combine_regions`, the
combiner every entry kind here is routed through).

`entries` supplies one entry per response part, in response part order;
each entry edits against its own base, never a dataset-level one. There
is no spec registry, so every entry carries its full identity and this
door reads no server-side state.

base_content_version.title: Base Content Version
base_content_version.description: the raw version a derived version (a full groupby collapse, a party-totals cut, or both) was rendered from. Null on every other version

rendering.title: Rendering
rendering.description: plain: a raw version, which is also what a groupby sum or a party-totals cut that left the frame unchanged is stored under. groupby: a collapse, summed by `groupby`, of the frame or of its party-totals cut when `without_party_totals` is true. without_party_totals: the frame without its party totals, unsummed. not_recorded: a derived version with no linked file recording its options

groupby.description: the groupby a collapse was summed by, as its file's rendering records it. Null unless `rendering` is groupby

without_party_totals.title: Without Party Totals
without_party_totals.description: true when the derived version's frame leaves out the group totals of its open party roles, as its file's rendering records it. Absent when false

enrichment_stamp.title: Enrichment Stamp
enrichment_stamp.description: the `enrichment_stamp` a file of this version holding party-kind cells, rendered now, carries (`ArtifactEntryModel.enrichment_stamp`): the answering code index's digest, the page's `enrichment_stamp`, when the version's frame holds a party role. Absent when it holds none, since a file of it then holds no party-kind cell and carries no stamp under any code index. A version that stored neither an output profile nor a party-free link lists the digest

enrichment_stamp.title: Enrichment Stamp
enrichment_stamp.description: the digest of the party kinds, classes and whole-total markers the answering code index holds, the one a file rendered now carries (`ArtifactEntryModel.enrichment_stamp`). A frame naming a file that asks for a party-kind column adds it to its name, so a frame named under another stamp does not match

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: stored versions that are not revoked, newest first

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: continues the list after this page's last version; null when complete

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: true when this page reaches the end of the list

DateRange.title: DateRange
DateRange.description: The first and last dates of the points an answer serves for a StatVar.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: contract schema version; exactly 1 for v1. Required on every response.

query_echo.description: what the response was understood to be answering

diagnostics.description: run health, warnings, timing, build stamp

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: discriminator for a response to a question search does not answer

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: why search declined: 'out_of_scope' when no part of the question asks for a published statistic about a place, a population or a financial flow; 'requires_analysis' when the subject is in scope but the question asks for an argument and names no data to show

scope.description: the place the question named, when it named a country

DeclinedAnswer.title: DeclinedAnswer
DeclinedAnswer.description: A resolve response to a question search does not answer.

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. Two parts marked separate that resolve to one reading carry the same spec_id and stay two parts. False, the default, is omitted

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order, and a candidates part's then closes with its assumptions clause. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

entity_refs.title: Entity Refs
entity_refs.description: the binding of each entity of `restatement`, one per restatement.entities row, in row order, so a client can tell which node a text such as 'G7' bound. A response field kept off `restatement`, which posts back unchanged. The binding is the one the answer reads: for a candidates part, the elected reading's; for a part folded into an earlier part's spec, its own. [] when `restatement` is null or names no entity

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

departures.title: Departures
departures.description: every way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, ordered by how much each changes the number: closest_match, measure_not_applied, operation_not_applied, breakdown_not_applied, entity_unavailable, year_unavailable, modelled_values, group_read_as_members, whole_total_read, whole_total_unpublished, direction_discarded, direction_inferred, scope_limited. [] when the answer is what was asked. A client that renders its own sentence reads them here; each one's text also closes the sentence that carries this part (see Departure.text). A warning on the same part reports run health and stays separate

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: every value the engine filled that the request did not ask for, in clause order. Declared defaults come first, in the order of the Spec's trace.slot_filters, then open roles, then the place scope. A declared default is a slot the request left open that its code system's or shape's declared default fixed, named by the bound code's full label. An open role is a flow role no request word asked for, read across every entity on it with data. It is either a role the role scope default filled (resolved.scope on that axis), whatever its member count, served as one series per member where the shape declares the role, or a role the heading states with no entity of its own ('from 164 providers', 'owed to all creditors'), served as the total over its members. A role the identity binds in entities or lists in open_roles, that one of the part's operations runs over ('top 5 donors'), or that the request's words asked every member of ('all donors'), is asked. The place scope is a request that named no place, read across every place with data. Every door fills assumptions. A definite part reads them from its Spec, a candidates part carries the items every list in CandidatesPart.reading_assumptions holds alike, text included, and no_data and unsupported parts carry []. A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts every slot bound, so its part states the items of the entry's assumptions echo that still hold (see ResubmitIdentityEntry.assumptions), and a candidates entry reads each reading with its candidate's echo (see ResubmitCandidate.assumptions). The sentence that carries this part closes with them as one segment='assumption' clause ('Assumed: official development assistance; every provider.'), after its departures. [] when the answer fills nothing

spec.description: the resolved Spec answering this part. Parts whose specs share a spec_id are one reading of the data, the same series, entities and years. A later part that folds into an earlier part's spec carries binding_folded. A part posted with separate: true never folds and keeps its own part, so two separate parts can carry one spec_id by request. Parts sharing a spec_id can differ in assumptions, so a client never dedupes parts by spec_id

DefinitePart.title: DefinitePart
DefinitePart.description: One unambiguous answer was resolved for this part.

DefinitionMembersRequest.title: DefinitionMembersRequest
DefinitionMembersRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/datasets/{id}/members`. It may carry the canonical `definition` a
search response gives for `id`, so the route answers before any mint registers it.

A registered id needs no `definition`. A supplied one is admitted as a mint admits a
`spec_id` sidecar: `definition.spec_id` must equal the path id, and the identity must hash
to it. Nothing is written.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: the identity-core document, shaped as search.models.identity.BaseIdentity and published at GET /api/search/schema

DefinitionOptionsRequest.title: DefinitionOptionsRequest
DefinitionOptionsRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/datasets/{id}/options`. It carries the canonical `definition` a search
response gives for `id`, so the options route answers for an id no mint has registered.

The route admits and registers the definition as a `spec_id` mint registers its sidecar.
`definition.spec_id` must equal the path id, and the identity must hash to it.

DefinitionResponse.title: DefinitionResponse
DefinitionResponse.description:
The register door's response: the verified
identity, echoed back whole.

DefinitionText.title: GraphDefinitionText
DefinitionText.description: The graph's prose for one part of a definition.

code.title: Code
code.description: what kind of departure this is. 'closest_match': the answer shows the nearest measure the graph holds, not the one asked; a client draws a muted 'Closest match:' lead before the heading, and on a candidates part, whose readings stand in for a measure with no data, once before the first reading. 'measure_not_applied': a named measure qualifier was not applied. 'operation_not_applied': an operation the request named (a share, a ranking) was not run, so the amounts behind it are shown. 'breakdown_not_applied': a breakdown the request named was not applied, so the total is shown. 'entity_unavailable': an entity the request named holds no values in the series the answer reads, one departure per role; for a role the request named as a group, asked is the request's words for the group and the text counts the members without values; the text names any source holding values there that Search does not read. 'year_unavailable': a named year or range falls outside the years served. 'modelled_values': the served values are modelled or estimated. 'group_read_as_members': a named group was read as its member entities; on a flow role the text names the amounts the group's published total counts that no member holds, and, for a group whose published total is not its members' sum, says the source publishes its own figure for the group. 'whole_total_read': a flow side is read as its whole population, the total its source publishes for every party of that side (official donors (DAC) for 'official donors' or a donor side the request named nothing on or summed over; official and private donors (DAC) for 'all donors'); the text says what the total holds and how to list the side's members: in the question's words ('by donor') on the raw_text door, with open_roles on the others. 'whole_total_unpublished': the request named a whole population ('all donors', 'all recipients') on a side whose dataset publishes no total of it and holds no party outside it, so the side is left unnamed and the answer covers every party the dataset holds there; asked is the request's words, and the text names the dataset. 'direction_discarded': a flow direction the request's own words named was not applied. 'direction_inferred': a place the request named without a direction is read on the one direction that holds data, which over names. 'scope_limited': a no_data answer's check covered only values the engine chose, which the request did not name; its text names only what the check covered ('This check covered only ODA.')

binding_ref.title: Binding Ref
binding_ref.description: the identity binding whose edit clears this departure ('when:' for a year, 'how:<property dcid>' for a measure value, 'where:' or 'origin:' for a role's entities, 'unit:' for the price basis); null for a departure no binding edit clears, such as an operation the engine does not run. A client links the departure to the sentence token carrying the same binding_ref when the plan has one; a candidates or no_data plan, and a how slot the heading leaves silent, may carry no such token

asked.title: Asked
asked.description: what the request named, in its own wording; null when it named nothing

shown.title: Shown
shown.description: what the answer shows instead, as the heading states it; null when nothing

text.title: Text
text.description: the departure as one or two short sentences for people: 'You asked for 2030. The data ends in 2024, so this shows 1973 to 2024.' On a no_data part no text claims the part shows anything. The envelope's composed sentence carries the same text as a segment='departure' token after its part's heading and byline, and so does the rendered_sentence of a part that is not definite

Departure.title: Departure
Departure.description:
One way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, stated
for people in `text` and for code in `code`, `asked`, and `shown`.

Departures live on the part (`_PartBase.departures`).
`spec.resolved.rendered_sentence` states what the answer is, and a
departure states how that differs from the request that produced it.

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: the deployment default policy's own id

DeploymentFacetPolicy.title: DeploymentFacetPolicy
DeploymentFacetPolicy.description:
This deployment's own default-facet policy: what an unbound facet
axis falls back to once `default_facet_policies_live` (a graph-declared,
per-StatVar policy) is `false`. See `docs/datasets-facet-policy.md`.

DescribedProperty.title: DescribedProperty
DescribedProperty.description: The open dimension a values page lists, and its label (`null` where none is known).

DescribedValue.title: DescribedValue
DescribedValue.description:
One value of an open dimension, its label (`null` where none is known), and how many of
the version's variables with data hold it.

DescriptionValuesPage.title: DescriptionValuesPage
DescriptionValuesPage.description:
One page of `GET /api/datasets/{id}/{content_version}/description/values`: the values
the version's record holds for one open dimension, most variables first, ties ordered by
dcid. `next_cursor` continues the list after the page's last value and is `null` on its
last page, where `complete` is true.

DiagnosticModel.title: DiagnosticModel
DiagnosticModel.description:
One manifest diagnostic: a fact about how this response was produced that a developer
reads and a dataset's description leaves out, since it states nothing about the data.
`processing_level_undeclared` and `origin_catalogue_stale` are the codes it carries.

engine_build.title: Engine Build
engine_build.description: the commit sha the image was built from, the same value the x-dfo-commit response header carries; distinct from schema_version

trace_id.title: Trace Id
trace_id.description: this request's trace_id, shared verbatim with every RFC 9457 problem-details body and the SSE stream's `done` event

llm_usage.title: Llm Usage
llm_usage.description: per-request LLM token counts {input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens}, plus {jev_input_tokens, jev_output_tokens} when Jev answered a call

timed_out.title: Timed Out
timed_out.description: True when the pipeline's soft deadline truncated this result to a partial response; False when it ran to completion. None on the SSE response event (whose `done` event carries the authoritative flag instead) -- only resolve_async's buffered ResolveResponse populates this, since a buffered caller has no `done` event of its own to read.

Diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
Diagnostics.description: Run health, warnings, timing, and build stamp.

DimensionNoun.title: DimensionNoun
DimensionNoun.description: What one member of a flow dimension is called, and several of them.

member.title: Member
member.description: the wire path the document fills

line.title: Line
line.description: 1-based line in the decoded document where the problem starts, or null

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: the template rule the document breaks

DocumentErrorEntry.title: DocumentErrorEntry
DocumentErrorEntry.description:
A Markdown document the source carries that this door could not serve.
The member it fills is empty and named in `gaps`.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: the rows the definition's series serve: one per series and date, totals included. A long-layout CSV or XLSX keeps the rows where a role the Datasets options document lists in long_layout_totals holds a total out of its main table, so that table can hold fewer. Null when it could understate: a served member the coverage artifact does not hold

rows_exact.title: Rows Exact
rows_exact.description: true when rows equals the mint's coverage.rows. Under a unit request rows counts only the rows the conversion keeps: at constant prices each entity's rows in the years its deflator holds, none when it lacks the base year. False when rows is an upper bound: a unit request whose conversion cannot be read from the loaded conversion tables (none loaded, served facets under several recipes or in a unit that is no currency, or no single deflator role), or a series whose facets carry no complete date list. False when rows is null

series.title: Series
series.description: the series in the file: distinct (StatVar, entities) with a point, the mint's series_count. Null when rows is null

window.description: the first and last years of the file's points; null when rows is null

licence.description: the licence of the one provenance the answer serves, from the origin catalogue; null when it serves several, or the catalogue names no single licence for it

DownloadFacts.title: DownloadFacts
DownloadFacts.description:
What a Datasets mint of this Spec's definition writes in its default file (no
grouping), known before the first download. Rows and series count what the answer's
read plan serves over the identity's whole window: every year for no window, the
range for a range, and each series' latest year for `latest`.

label.title: Label
label.description: the licence's name: the `name` of the licenseType node the provenances of the provenance's source-index entry agree on

DownloadLicence.title: DownloadLicence
DownloadLicence.description:
The licence of the provenance a Spec's file cites. Its terms page is on the
provenance's source page.

EnrichmentOptionModel.title: EnrichmentOptionModel
EnrichmentOptionModel.description:
One `(entity column, field)` enrichment this deployment enables,
with `token` naming the exact `{column}_{field}` the `columns` option
accepts to request it.

parties.title: Parties
parties.description: entities with figures of their own

private.title: Private
private.description: the parties whose class is private, a subset of parties

totals.title: Totals
totals.description: entities that hold other entities' figures

residual.title: Residual
residual.description: entities holding figures no other entity does

unclassified.title: Unclassified
unclassified.description: entities the code index does not list

EntityCounts.title: GraphAvailabilityEntityCounts
EntityCounts.description: The distinct entities in one role, split by their kind in the code index.

EntityCoverage.title: EntityCoverage
EntityCoverage.description: How many of the window's periods one ranked entity holds.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the group's own graph node, when the graph holds one; null otherwise

label.title: Label
label.description: the group's name as the request gave it, plain text

entity_type.title: Entity Type
entity_type.description: the graph type of the group's own node, e.g. Continent, UNGeoRegion, ContinentalUnion; null when the graph holds no node for the group

total.title: Total
total.description: the party the dataset publishes as the group's total, which the role binds in place of the members (DACAfrica for Africa); null when the role binds the members

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: the membership registry's id for a group the graph holds no node for, e.g. groups/OECD.DAC.Region.Asia; null when ref is set or the group is no registry group

whole_of.title: Whole Of
whole_of.description: the classes of party the role's whole population covers, sorted: official, private or residual, e.g. ["official"] for Official Donors, Total, which holds every official donor and no private one; absent for any other group

side_classes.title: Side Classes
side_classes.description: for a role read as its whole population, the classes of party, totals aside, the answer's dataset publishes on that side, sorted, e.g. ["official", "private", "residual"] for donors in DAC2a; a class here and not in whole_of, such as "private", is outside the total. Absent for any other group. Derived from the identity on every answer; a posted value is ignored

EntityGroup.title: EntityGroup
EntityGroup.description:
A named group whose members fill one entity role, as the request named it
("EU member states"). The members themselves are the role's dcids in
`BaseIdentity.entities`. This records only that they were asked for as one
group, so the heading can say "the 27 EU member states" after any edit that
keeps the role's members. A group the graph holds no node for, read from the
membership registry ("Asia (DAC)"), names the registry's id for it in
`group_id`, so a resubmit restores it and the total its dataset publishes for it.
A group whose `ref` is a continent or subregion
that the membership policy holds or omits (`MembershipPolicy.holds_region`)
reads as its countries ("the 54 countries in Africa"), whatever its graph
type. `entity_type` is informational, and the reading keys on `ref`. When
the role binds the total its dataset publishes
for the group ("Africa (DAC)") in place of the members, `total` names that
party and the role's one dcid is it. A role read as the whole population of
its side, the source's total of every party there ("Official Donors, Total")
or a union of such totals ("all donors including private"), states the
classes of party that population covers in `whole_of`, and the classes the answer's
dataset publishes on that side in `side_classes`; a resubmit derives both from the
identity and the code index, whatever it posts. A Spec serves its groups on
`ResolvedSpec.entity_groups`, and a resubmit posts them beside the identity
(`ResubmitIdentityEntry.entity_groups`, `ResubmitCandidate.entity_groups`).

entity_ref.title: Entity Ref
entity_ref.description: dcid of the currently-bound directional entity; joins to an entry in SentenceToken.entity_refs. None means this role axis is open -- no entity is bound on it, and `options` is this axis's own candidate member set rather than a set the current binding could be swapped among. An open role axis omits this key entirely on both the buffered body and the SSE entity_options event, rather than emitting null -- the opposite of SlotOption.coverage's own explicit-null convention on that same SSE channel

role.description: the flow axis these candidates apply to; present even when entity_ref is omitted so a selected candidate can be posted under the same identity.entities role

options.title: Options
options.description: candidate entities, reusing SlotOption for shape parity with slot_options

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: true when options is capped or deliberately count-only, so it is not the complete known candidate set; false when every known candidate is listed

source.title: Source
source.description: 'seed' for a hand-curated candidate set; 'observed' for candidates already confirmed while resolving this flow axis

EntityOptions.title: EntityOptions
EntityOptions.description:
Candidates for one directional entity axis.

Parallel to SlotOptions, but for a directional *entity* (an observation
endpoint) rather than a constraint-property value. A role-bearing flow may
expose either its origin or destination axis here when that axis was left
open. The entry's ``role`` is the routing key a client uses to promote a
selected candidate into ``identity.entities`` on a dataset_resubmit entry.

EntityRef.title: GraphResolveEntity
EntityRef.description:
A reference with its kind. `kind` is `null` only for a `not_held` entity, which the
graph holds no node to classify.

text.title: Text
text.description: the entity text, equal to restatement.entities[i].text, where i is this entry's position in Part.entity_refs

refs.title: Refs
refs.description: the refs the part's answer binds for `text`: a place gives its node; a group, continent or subregion bound as itself gives its own node, or the total its dataset publishes for it (G7 bound as GroupOfSeven); one bound as its members gives the set's own ref first (its node, else that total, else its registry id) and then the members, sorted. [] for an ambiguous text, one that resolved to no node or a node the answer does not bind, and every text of a part refused before its places were bound

EntityRefs.title: EntityRefs
EntityRefs.description: The graph nodes one entity row of a part's restatement binds in the answer.

years.title: Years
years.description: the years left out, as runs of consecutive years, `1990-2001` or `2004`

EntityYearsModel.title: EntityYearsModel
EntityYearsModel.description:
One entity a conversion left rows out of, and the years of those rows
(`materialise.codes.EntityYears`).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: superseded_by_dfo: an upstream copy of a dataset DFO imports. superseded_by_un_system: a UN System Data Commons agency's series replace it

Exclusion.title: Exclusion
Exclusion.description:
A provenance a base source holds that this deployment does not admit, because
another Data Commons supersedes it.

added.title: Added
added.description: descendant codes admitted beyond the slot's own bound value(s), in the code index's descendant-walk order. Never empty -- a slot whose expansion added nothing carries no Expansion at all (Slot.expansion is None), rather than one with added=[]

Expansion.title: Expansion
Expansion.description:
Codes a hierarchical value/set binding resolved to beyond its own bound
value(s): the descendant codes admitted by walking the code index's
`specializationOf` closure for a dimension the index declares
`hierarchical` (code_index.query.CodeIndex.descendants).

Additive only. Never a substitute for `binding`, and never fed into spec
identity -- `BindingValue`/`BindingSet` are the sole identity-bearing wire
form (see Slot.expansion's own docstring for why: identity is minted from
`BindingSet.values`, built from the query's own drafted values, before
resolution ever widens them). `added` never repeats a dcid already in the
binding's own value(s); it holds only what expansion contributed on top.

FacetItem.title: GraphFacetItem
FacetItem.description:
One facet of a variable, as the `facets` list relation serves it. `ref` is the facet id,
which hashes the facet's metadata.

FacetNationalCurrencyBinding.title: FacetNationalCurrencyBinding
FacetNationalCurrencyBinding.description:
The unit axis bound to each entity's own currency: at each entity `role`
binds, the facets whose unit is the one currency the graph's
`nationalCurrencyOf` names for it, served as published and never converted.
The conversion request naming the same role (`UnitCurrencyRole`) converts
each row into that currency instead.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the facet axis this option set belongs to (see FacetAxis)

options.title: Options
options.description: candidate values seen on the resolved candidates' own unfiltered observation facets, ranked by in-window observation-point count descending then ref ascending; a dcid the graph can't label falls back to the dcid itself as its own label rather than being dropped -- every value here already came off a confirmed observation facet, unlike a curated seed candidate. On the measurementMethod and unit axes, an option with no value.ref stands for the facets that declare no value on the axis, as Data Commons omits the member; it is listed only beside a declared value, ranks last among equal counts, and is pinned by posting identity.facets.<axis> as {state: 'value', ref: null}

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: true when options is bounded by SEARCH_MAX_OPTIONS rather than the full distinct set observed

source.title: Source
source.description: always 'observed' -- a facet axis has no curated seed taxonomy

FacetOptions.title: FacetOptions
FacetOptions.description:
The candidate set one facet axis (see ResolvedFacet) was chosen from:
every distinct value seen on the resolved candidates' own observation
facets, so a client can offer "what else could I ask for" alongside the
served answer.

Parallel to SlotOptions/EntityOptions, reusing SlotOption for shape
parity. Unlike either, source is always "observed" -- a facet axis has
no curated seed taxonomy -- and no option here ever carries a populated
SlotOption.coverage: there is no separate confirm step for a facet
option, the observed count already ranks the list.

FacetRefBinding.title: FacetRefBinding
FacetRefBinding.description:
A facet axis bound to a specific ref. Every axis accepts this form;
the unit axis alone also accepts `FacetUnitRequestBinding`, the
conversion-request form (`currency`/`prices`/`base_year`), and
`FacetNationalCurrencyBinding`. A null `ref` binds the facets that declare
no value on the axis, and only `NULL_REF_FACET_AXES` accept it.

changed.title: Changed
changed.description: the patch's own changed field names, empty for a create or a no-op write

series.title: Series
series.description: every visible series this revision resolves, capped

series_cut.title: Series Cut
series_cut.description: how many series the series cap and the token cap together dropped from this summary

window.description: this component's own [start, end] period window, null where its type defines none

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: this component's own unit, the value its resolved payload carries: a unit's graph name (its ref when the graph has none), a converted unit, or a composed unit. A line_chart or bar_chart reports its first series' unit and a table the unit every row shares. Null where the type defines none, the rows declare none, or a table's rows differ.

change.title: Change
change.description: the stat_card's derived comparison between its two basis periods, null for every other member and for a stat_card whose intent carries no change

source_refs.title: Source Refs
source_refs.description: every distinct raw provenance ref a source_card's frame carries. It is null for every other member.

defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.description: the choices this component made where its intent left one open, empty when it made none

FactSummaryModel.title: FactSummaryModel
FactSummaryModel.description: The closed, token-capped fact summary a revision reports.

id.title: Id
id.description: this series' own id, null when none could be assigned

label.title: Label
label.description: this series' own display label

point_count.title: Point Count
point_count.description: how many of this series' points carry an observed value

first_value.title: First Value
first_value.description: this series' earliest observed value, formatted, null when it has none

last_value.title: Last Value
last_value.description: this series' latest observed value, formatted, null when it has none

FactSummarySeriesEntry.title: FactSummarySeriesEntry
FactSummarySeriesEntry.description:
One `fact_summary.series[]` entry. It reports one visible series'
identity, point count and formatted boundary values.

frame.description: the named frame, which is its rendering's current one

values.title: Values
values.description: this dimension's own values matching the query

matched_count.title: Matched Count
matched_count.description: how many of this dimension's values matched the query

FrameDimensionMatch.title: FrameDimensionMatch
FrameDimensionMatch.description:
One dimension of a frame's query-filtered view (`?query=` given,
`dimension` absent). Its values are filtered to those matching the
query.

total_count.title: Total Count
total_count.description: this dimension's own value count before capping

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: whether this dimension's values list was capped

plural.title: Plural
plural.description: whether this frame's series hold more than one value of this dimension, a null counting as one; the estimates continuing a series hold its method, so they leave measurementMethod not plural

FrameDimensionSummary.title: FrameDimensionSummary
FrameDimensionSummary.description:
One dimension of a frame's structural view (`GET .../frames/{...}`
with neither `dimension` nor `query` given). Its values are capped to
the per-dimension listing cap.

values.title: Values
values.description: every value this dimension carries, uncapped, or only the values matching `query` when it is given

total_count.title: Total Count
total_count.description: how many values this dimension carries, or how many match `query` when it is given

FrameDimensionValuesResponse.title: FrameDimensionValuesResponse
FrameDimensionValuesResponse.description:
`GET /api/presentation/frames/{spec_id}/{content_version}?dimension=`'s
body. It reports one dimension's full value list, read fresh and
uncapped. Given alongside `?query=`, `values` and `total_count`
describe only the values matching the query.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: every dimension this frame declares, filtered

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: this frame's own [start, end] period coverage, null if it has none

FrameFilteredViewResponse.title: FrameFilteredViewResponse
FrameFilteredViewResponse.description:
`GET /api/presentation/frames/{spec_id}/{content_version}?query=`'s
body (`dimension` absent). It reports every dimension this frame
declares, filtered to values matching the query, counts kept.

frame.description: the current frame of the named frame's rendering

operation_id.title: Operation Id
operation_id.description: the queued rebuild, pollable on the operations route

retry_after_s.title: Retry After S
retry_after_s.description: seconds to wait before calling again

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: this frame's own [start, end] period coverage, null if it has none

series_count.title: Series Count
series_count.description: how many distinct series this frame resolves

FrameStructuralViewResponse.title: FrameStructuralViewResponse
FrameStructuralViewResponse.description:
`GET /api/presentation/frames/{spec_id}/{content_version}`'s body
with neither `dimension` nor `query` given. It reports the frame's own
structural view, every dimension capped.

Freshness.title: Freshness
Freshness.description:
A source's own refresh cadence, read from DCP provenance arcs that imports populate
unevenly: `dc/base/WHO_COVID19` carries both `sourceReleaseFrequency` and
`automaticRefreshType`, `dc/base/BIS_CentralBankPolicyRate` only the second, and
`dc/base/WHO_GHO` neither. Nullability is the contract.

`release_frequency` is the raw `sourceReleaseFrequency` ISO 8601 duration (`P1M`);
`release_frequency_label` is `materialise.cadence.cadence_label`'s display label for it
(`Monthly`), or the raw token when that module does not recognise it.

`refresh_type` is `automaticRefreshType`'s value: how this deployment refreshes the
source, such as `GCPCloudRunAutomaticRefresh`, or the sentinel `NoAutomaticRefresh`.

label.title: Label
label.description: plain-language display name, read from the graph

GraphRef.title: GraphRef
GraphRef.description: Every graph identifier in the contract.

schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.description: JSON Schema of each served request and response body, keyed by name

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: path of this surface's capability document

label.title: Label
label.description: the node's name; for a Provenance, its parent Dataset's name where it has one. Null, and named in gaps, when the graph gives none

types.title: Types
types.description: the node's typeOf values, as the graph holds them

description.title: Description
description.description: the node's prose in the graph; null when it has none

links.title: Links
links.description: each list relation the node has, mapped to its route; empty when none

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: the member path of every value this door cannot know

built_from.title: Built From
built_from.description: the build of each table the response read

levels.title: Levels
levels.description: code system -> depth: roll each kept code up to its ancestor at that depth (0 = root codes); a code shallower than the depth stays as itself, under its own label

GroupbyOptions.title: GroupbyOptions
GroupbyOptions.description:
`options.groupby`: a safe roll-up that keeps exactly the axes named
in `by`, one row per distinct combination of their values. Every other
graph-declared summable axis a frame decoded is summed away, `stat_var`
included. `by` names what a caller wants to see, the opposite of
`groupby_sum`'s own "collapse this axis" reading. `sum` is the only op
this closed reshape list allows.

Every `by` entry names a code system some deployment declaration marks
summable, a role/entity column (`materialise.roles.KNOWN_ROLE_NAMES`),
`stat_var`, or a column every frame carries regardless of shape; any
other name refuses `rollup_not_summable`
(`datasets_api.groupby.refuse_unknown_by_axes`). A declared axis this
frame's StatVars do not decode is left out of the collapse set
(`datasets_api.groupby.collapse_axes`).

`levels` rolls a kept hierarchical axis up to one depth of its parent
chain before the sum: each code becomes its ancestor at that depth, and
depth 0 is the root codes. Each key must also appear in `by`, and must
be one of the capabilities document's `groupby_level_axes`
(`datasets_api.render.check_options_supported`).

GroupbyOptionsModel.title: GroupbyOptionsModel
GroupbyOptionsModel.description:
`axes` names the axes a `groupby.by` request may keep: every other
declared-summable axis a frame decoded is collapsed into it. Empty
while `state` is `unavailable`.

year.title: Year
year.description: the year the counts are for. For a latest window it is the elected year: of the three calendar years ending at the newest year a variable's series hold, at or before the year the coverage artifact was built, the newest one that at least half as many series hold as the fullest of the three, and with several variables the newest year any of them elects. For a named window it is the latest year any served series has an observation inside the window

year_named.title: Year Named
year_named.description: whether the request itself named a year or a range of years, rather than defaulting to one, independent of whether those years include the shown `year`

named_window.description: the year or years the request named: equal bounds for one year, an absent bound for an open range; null when no year was named. The counts are for `year` alone, whatever this window holds

observations.title: Observations
observations.description: exact observation count across served series in year

series.title: Series
series.description: exact series count with an observation in year

role_counts.title: Role Counts
role_counts.description: distinct dcid count per role active in year, keyed by the graph's own role property dcid (e.g. financingProvider, financingRecipient) -- never by a donor/recipient label, so the wire stays aligned with Data Commons' own names

recent_years.title: Recent Years
recent_years.description: the counts for three calendar years, newest first, so a newest year with far fewer series than the years before it reads as incomplete. For a latest window they are raw counts over every series the answer holds, ending at the newest year any of them holds at or before the year the coverage artifact was built, or at the newest year any holds when none holds a year that early; `year` is one of the three: the newest year a variable heads, which is the year it elected or, for a variable that elects none, such as one of monthly data, its newest year at or before the build year. When no variable holds a year that early, each heads its newest year. `observations`, `series` and `role_counts` count only the variables heading it. For a named window they end at `year`, the first entry repeats `observations`, `series` and `role_counts`, and the earlier years count whether or not `named_window` reaches them. A year with no data is kept with zero counts. The list stops at the first year the coverage artifact represents, so it can hold fewer than three entries

Headline.title: Headline
Headline.description:
The exact, one-year summary of a role-bearing answer's own served
population: the year `CoverageIndex.headline` (series_coverage) heads the
answer with, whether that year was the one the question named, the exact
observation and series count in that year alone, and how many distinct dcids
each role carries in it. `series_coverage.index.Headline`'s own docstring is
the source of truth for why `observations` and `series` are always equal
under this schema.

The counts are those of the year the answer's read plan serves. Under a `latest`
window that is the year its variables elect (`CoverageIndex.elected_years`), which
the preview and a mint of the Spec serve too. Under a named window it is the latest
year with data in that window, so a question naming 2015 to 2020 counts the latest
of those years with data. `named_window` carries the years it named.

Attached to every role-bearing answer (named-destination confirmed and
open-axis discovered alike), never to a non-role-bearing one: coverage
only exists for role-bearing series (series_coverage.schema's own scope
note), and computing this is a free in-memory bitmask operation, not a
network read, so there is no population-size reason to withhold it from
a narrow answer the way the per-series preview stays capped at 20
regardless of how broad the answer is.

year.title: Year
year.description: the calendar year these counts are for

observations.title: Observations
observations.description: exact observation count across served series in year

series.title: Series
series.description: exact series count with an observation in year

role_counts.title: Role Counts
role_counts.description: distinct dcid count per role active in year, keyed by the graph's own role property dcid; a role with no dcid in the year is absent

HeadlineYear.title: HeadlineYear
HeadlineYear.description:
The exact counts for one calendar year of a role-bearing answer's served
population: observations and series with an observation in it, and how many
distinct dcids each role carries. A year with no data counts zero.

build.title: Build
build.description: the commit sha the image was built from, the same value the x-dfo-commit response header carries, "unknown" on a checkout run with no DFO_BUILD_COMMIT set

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description: `GET /healthz`'s own response body, shared across every surface.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the bound dcid, denoting that code alone

IdentityBindingExact.title: IdentityBindingExact
IdentityBindingExact.description:
A single bound dcid, denoting that code alone -- never its subtree,
even where the code is a hierarchical (non-leaf) code (see
`docs/identity-v1.md` in `spec-kit` for the denotation rule: `value`
denotes a hierarchical code's whole subtree, `exact` denotes the code
alone). Slot-only: `_build_facet_binding` refuses `exact` on a facet.
No engine `Binding` arm maps onto this state and no minting site
produces it -- see `IdentityBinding`'s own docstring.

refs.title: Refs
refs.description: the bound dcids (dfo_spec_kit sorts and de-duplicates)

IdentityBindingSet.title: IdentityBindingSet
IdentityBindingSet.description: A bound dcid set, in the identity core's own binding wire shape.

IdentityBindingValue.title: IdentityBindingValue
IdentityBindingValue.description: A single bound dcid, in the identity core's own binding wire shape.

role.title: Role
role.description: the entity role whose bound entity's currency this request means

IdentityCurrencyRole.title: IdentityCurrencyRole
IdentityCurrencyRole.description:
The role-shaped form of a unit request's `currency`: the currency of
the entity bound to this spec role, resolved per row. Field-for-field mirror
of the identity core's own `_CURRENCY_ROLE_KEYS`/`_CURRENCY_ROLES`
(`dfo_spec_kit.identity`'s `_build_currency`, the object arm).

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: null: the facet declares no value on this axis

IdentityFacetValueAbsent.title: IdentityFacetValueAbsent
IdentityFacetValueAbsent.description:
A measurementMethod or unit facet bound to no declared value:
`{"state": "value", "ref": null}` asks for the facets that declare no value
on the axis, the ones Data Commons serves without that member. An unbound
axis admits every facet; this binding admits only those without a value.
Mirrors the identity core's null facet ref (`docs/identity-v1.md` in
`spec-kit`). `ref` serialises as `null` even under `exclude_none`, since
the identity core refuses a value binding with neither `ref` nor `request`.

IdentityFacetValueRequest.title: IdentityFacetValueRequest
IdentityFacetValueRequest.description:
A unit-axis facet bound via the request form: "serve whatever facet
honours this completed currency/prices/base_year request" rather than a
literal graph ref. `state` reuses the value-state spelling since this is
still a single-valued binding to the identity core -- `request` is what
distinguishes it from `IdentityBindingValue`'s `ref` form (see
`_facet_binding_tag`, this union's discriminator).

IdentityShapeDenominatorRef.title: IdentityShapeDenominatorRef
IdentityShapeDenominatorRef.description: The described arm's `measurement_denominator`, resolved to a dcid.

unresolved.title: Unresolved
unresolved.description: always the literal true -- the arc exists but names no dcid

IdentityShapeDenominatorUnresolved.title: IdentityShapeDenominatorUnresolved
IdentityShapeDenominatorUnresolved.description:
The described arm's `measurement_denominator`, present on the graph but
never resolved to a dcid (e.g. a dcid-less ProvisionalNode) -- distinct
from the member being absent entirely, which means no denominator arc
exists at all.

IdentityShapePin.title: IdentityShapePin
IdentityShapePin.description:
The pinned-ask arm of the identity core's `shape` union
(`kind: "stat_var"`): a single StatVar dcid, minted by Datasets'
statvar_set. See `BaseIdentity`'s cross-member validator -- when this arm
is chosen, `slots` must be empty.

stat_type.title: Stat Type
stat_type.description: the graph statType dcid, e.g. measuredValue

measurement_qualifier.title: Measurement Qualifier
measurement_qualifier.description: the graph measurementQualifier dcid, present only when the measured property is qualified

measurement_denominator.title: Measurement Denominator
measurement_denominator.description: the graph measurementDenominator, present only on a ratio or per-capita measure: {'ref': dcid} when resolved, {'unresolved': true} when the arc exists but names no dcid

IdentityShapeSchema.title: IdentityShapeSchema
IdentityShapeSchema.description:
The described-ask arm of the identity core's `shape` union
(`kind: "statvar_schema"`): up to five sparse schema members mapping 1:1
onto Search's FiveTuple (see `engine.shape.identity_shape_for`, the
adapter that builds this from a ShapeDraft's or a grounded wire Shape's
five-tuple dcids). Minted by Search for every standard and family shape.

Every member is optional and sparse -- an absent member contributes no
bytes, the same sparse rule the facets map follows -- but an arm
describing nothing is invalid: at least one member must be present (see
`_at_least_one_schema_member`).

IdentitySlot.title: IdentitySlot
IdentitySlot.description:
One what/how slot's identity contribution: property dcid + binding state.

Never a where/when/source slot: `where` is carried by entity roles instead,
`when` is carried by `requested_window` instead, and `source` is carried by
`facets.provenance` instead -- all three would otherwise hash resolved
graph state rather than what was actually asked. Every IdentitySlot here
carries a real constraint property by construction of the shape grammar.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: the requested currency, upper-case ISO 4217 (e.g. 'USD'), or a role object

base_year.title: Base Year
base_year.description: required exactly when prices=='constant'; absent when prices=='current'

IdentityUnitRequest.title: IdentityUnitRequest
IdentityUnitRequest.description:
A completed unit-conversion request, in the identity core's own wire
shape (`dfo_spec_kit.identity`'s `_build_unit_request`) -- legal only
inside a unit-axis facet binding's `request` member
(`IdentityFacetValueRequest`; see `BaseIdentity`'s model validator, which
refuses this form on any other axis).

Field-for-field mirror of the identity core's own `_UNIT_REQUEST_KEYS`
schema: `currency` is upper-case ISO 4217 or a role object naming
the spec role whose bound entity's currency to use (see
`IdentityCurrency`; the identity core NFC-normalises a string spelling
but does not case-fold, so a lower-case currency refuses here rather
than silently normalising to a different meaning at hash time), `prices`
is current (nominal) or constant (real, anchored to
`base_year`), and `base_year` is present exactly when `prices=="constant"`
-- both directions enforced below, matching the identity core's own
`invalid_unit_request` pair of checks. `base_year` is `StrictInt`,
matching `_require_integral_number`'s own exclusion of `bool` (a Python
`int` subclass) and of numeric strings -- a lax `int` field would coerce
JSON `true` to `1` and `"2023"` to `2023`, hashing a malformed request
under an unintended base year instead of refusing it. Under simultaneous
violations
(e.g. a lower-case currency together with a missing base_year) the two
layers can report a different invariant first: this model's per-field
`currency` pattern validates ahead of `_base_year_matches_prices` (a
`mode="after"` validator, which never runs once a field has already
failed), while the identity core checks `prices`-vs-`base_year` before
the currency regex. Same HTTP status/code either way -- message content
only.

IdentityWindowAll.title: IdentityWindowAll
IdentityWindowAll.description: No date signal was requested at all.

IdentityWindowLatest.title: IdentityWindowLatest
IdentityWindowLatest.description: An explicit latest-ask: re-resolve to whatever year is CURRENTLY latest.

IdentityWindowRange.title: IdentityWindowRange
IdentityWindowRange.description: A concrete requested date range; at least one bound is always present.

LeftOut.title: LeftOut
LeftOut.description:
One data gap: why some data was left out, how many, and of what. The caller's own
selection is a parameter and never appears here.

A `pooled_entities` count is of the distinct parties of one pooled role, named in `role`,
across all the step's inputs. Those parties are never among the entities the step kept.
Only that `of` takes a `role`, and it requires one.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: facts about how this response was produced, for developers: a citation whose sources declare no processing level, and an origin catalogue past its staleness limit. A version stores none; each response states its own

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: every servable artifact for this rendering, in a fixed order: every data artifact first, the series-statistics/1 artifact (rendering.statistics == 'series') last, if present. A caller selecting the data artifact should check rendering rather than take the first entry, but the order itself is a stable contract, not an accident of storage

series_coverage_stamp.title: Series Coverage Stamp
series_coverage_stamp.description: the series_coverage artifact stamp this request's sync-admission estimate was computed against, kept as lineage only. content_version is a pure function of the frame and does not fold this in. Not the same coverage as the 'coverage' field above (materialise.window.Coverage's row/dimension/window report)

retention.description: how long this version can still be fetched: the retention of the frame every file renders from (a derived version's base frame). Each door sets it on its response

Manifest.title: Manifest
Manifest.description:
`trace` stays a plain dict, since `materialise.trace.ManifestTrace.to_dict()`
is already this field's exact wire shape.

`series_count` is the number of distinct series this definition
resolves, as the version's description counts them (`statistics.SeriesFigures.series`): a
series and the estimates continuing it count once, though the statistics artifact holds a
row for each method. `None` means a version record minted before this field existed, whose old
inline `statistics` no fact carries. The per-series detail itself lives in the
`series-statistics/1` Parquet artifact every door that returns a
`Manifest` lists in `artifacts` whenever `series_count` is not `None`
(`datasets_api.render.render_and_store_series_statistics`), never
inline on this model.

`output_options` is `None` on a version record minted before the field
existed, the same convention `series_count` uses.

`prepared_at` is when this version was first prepared, written once at its
first mint and stored with it, so every re-mint and re-render reads the same
instant.

Matched.title: GraphResolveMatched
Matched.description:
The listed text the input matched, and whether it is the entity's name, an alias, or a
code. A phrase naming a group's members ("EU countries") matches as `alias`.

label.title: Label
label.description: the measure's noun phrase, such as `net disbursements`

Measure.title: GraphDefinitionMeasure
Measure.description: What the variable counts or sums, as the code index names it.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the declared measure-axis identifier (code_index.types.MeasureAxis.axis), e.g. 'measuredProperty' or a constraint-property dcid such as 'financialFlowType'

value.description: the value's dcid and the measure index's label for it, e.g. Gross

MeasureAxisValue.title: MeasureAxisValue
MeasureAxisValue.description:
One measure axis and the value a measure partition holds on it (see
ResolvedSpec.measure_axis_values).

MemberItem.title: GraphMemberItem
MemberItem.description:
One item of a list: its dcid and the owner's label for it, `null` where the owner holds
no name.

MembersEnvelope.title: MembersEnvelope
MembersEnvelope.description:
`POST /api/datasets/{id}/members`'s response: the members a mint of the spec serves,
resolved without materialising a frame.

`members` lists them sorted by `ref`, and `served_count` counts them.
`family_member_count` and `family_member_digest` state the whole population the identity
admits, before a broader member's dominated members are dropped, as a mint's
`trace.family_member_count` and `trace.family_member_digest` state it; both are `null`
when member resolution cannot state that population.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the node whose list this is

projection.description: the membership projection listed; null for a relation that takes none

as_of.title: As Of

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: the cursor for the next page; null when this page ends the list

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: whether the walk reached the end of a list the owner holds in full

total.title: Total
total.description: the list's length; null where the list is partial

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: the code of each way the list is partial

built_from.title: Built From
built_from.description: the build of each table the list read
