MembershipBlock.title: GraphMembershipBlock
MembershipBlock.description: A group's or region's membership under its declared authority.

description.title: Description
description.description: how the publisher collects and compiles the data, as CommonMark

MintOptions.title: MintOptions
MintOptions.description:
Rendering-only, never hashed into identity. `format`/`bundle`/`pivot`/
`columns`/`groupby`/`without_party_totals` are this deployment's live rendering surface. A
`groupby.by` entry names a code system some deployment declaration
marks summable, a role/entity column, `stat_var`, or a column every
frame carries regardless of shape; any other name refuses
`rollup_not_summable` (`datasets_api.groupby.refuse_unknown_by_axes`).
A declared axis this frame did not decode is simply absent from the
collapse-set computation, not an error (see
`datasets_api.groupby.collapse_axes`); an unsafe collapse refuses
`rollup_not_summable` too, naming the axis and precondition
(`materialise.reshape.groupby_sum`,
`datasets_api.groupby.refuse_stat_var_collision`,
`datasets_api.groupby.refuse_decode_gaps`). A `columns` entry naming a
recognised-but-disabled enrichment field refuses `capability_unavailable`.
`columns` selects the table and decoded columns it names. A list that names
only enrichment fields selects nothing: every default column stays,
decoded columns included, and the enrichments are added. A list that mixes
a table column with an enrichment selects. Without a pivot, a list that
names no decoded column keeps all of them, `status` is accepted and left
out, `<role>_label` is written by default (a list naming it keeps
`<role>`), and the written order follows the long layout
(`materialise.projection`) whatever order the list names.

`layout: "frame"` writes a bare parquet file in the frame layout instead
of the long layout: the frame's grammar columns as reshaped, with
decoded axes as `stat_var_<code_system>`, `status` kept, and a converted
unit as its JCS request text. `columns` then selects over those columns,
as it does for pivot output. It refuses with `bundle: true`, a `pivot`,
or a format other than parquet.

`without_party_totals: true` leaves out the rows whose party, on a flow party role the
served identity binds no entity on, the code index declares a group total
(`datasets_api.party_totals`). It runs on the frame before any reshape, so a `groupby`
sums members alone. A cut that leaves rows out mints a version of its own, as a `groupby`
collapse does; one that leaves nothing out serves the frame's own version.

MintRequest.title: MintRequest
MintRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/datasets`: one `input` and the render `options`.

NationalCurrency.title: GraphAvailabilityNationalCurrency
NationalCurrency.description: The units that are each covered place's own currency.

spec_id.title: Spec Id
spec_id.description: deterministic hash of (shape + canonical slot bindings); permalink-safe, dedup key, golden-comparison handle, cache key

definition.description: the canonical definition this Spec was resolved from: {schema_version, identity}, the same shape Unsupported.definition uses. definition.identity is the identity-core projection this spec_id was minted from, serialised once and never re-derived; hashing it reproduces spec_id by construction. Post definition.identity back byte-for-byte as ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity to edit this Spec. Directional entities remain nested in identity.entities.

resolved.description: the engine's report of what it did with the ask: stat_vars, entities, coverage, trace, and every other display/diagnostic field. Never hashed; see ResolvedSpec

relaxation.description: the definition part this suggestion relaxed, and the value(s) it dropped

NearestRealSpec.title: NearestRealSpec
NearestRealSpec.description:
A nearest_real suggestion: a full Spec found by relaxing one constraint
binding and re-confirming the result against the live graph.

Graph-re-confirmed only, never fabricated. See relaxation for which
binding was dropped to find it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: why nothing could be returned, in contract resolution order. "entity_not_resolved" means a named entity could not be resolved to a graph node; "entity_ambiguous" means a named entity matched more than one graph candidate and none could be preferred over the others, distinct from "entity_not_resolved", where no node matched at all; "entity_role_not_admitted" means a named entity resolved to exactly one graph node, but no role any candidate shape declares admits that node's graph type -- the entity is real, just not the kind of thing this query's data is reported for; "entity_set_too_large" means every named entity resolved, but the places the request names, counting the members of each group or region among them and summed over the roles they sit on, exceed what the engine binds in one request -- distinct from every other entity_* reason, where one entity, not the size of the set, is what failed; "variable_not_resolved" means no StatVar matched the variable text (e.g. an absent posted stat_var_dcid or entity, or no measure match at all); "role_not_resolved" means the query names a role the engine could not resolve; "unit_not_resolved" means the unit binder could not classify a token in the requested unit phrase against its lexicons; "no_matching_slice" means the measure matched fine, but the requested combination has no corresponding data series -- the constructed/derived variable does not exist in the graph at all. Covers an identity resubmit refine edit with no confirmable sibling StatVar for the edited slice, and a dev-finance scheme x purpose x recipient combination that was never published as a series, on raw-text and resubmit alike; "binding_mismatch" means the variable resolved and graph-confirmed StatVars exist, but none satisfies the requested slot bindings, either because a resolved value on a bound property mismatched or because the StatVar's value on a bound property is present but could not be read (an unresolvable dcid); distinct from "no_matching_slice" (the combination was never published at all) and "variable_not_resolved" (no StatVar matched at all); "denominator_not_available" means the query asks for a normalised form (per person, per area, a rate or a share) or names a denominator, and the matched series is not in that form or divides by another base; "no_observations" means a StatVar WAS confirmed to exist but has no observation at the resolved entity (it exists, but not data here); "facet_not_available" means observations exist at the entity, none under the requested facet values; "role_incompatible" means the role is real, and the StatVar does not declare it; "role_signature_incompatible" means the resolved StatVars carry incompatible role signatures and no partition into candidates was possible; "source_code_not_held" means no variable held under the part's source_code by a source search serves can answer the part: no served source holds the code, the part's sources exclude every source that does, or the code's variables cannot answer the part as asked; "source_code_ambiguous" means two of the part's sources hold its source_code; "source_code_shares_variable" means the source_code's variables answer other codes of its source too, so search cannot serve the code alone; "qualifier_not_bound" means the variable resolved to a series family, but a narrowing term the request's text named bound no constraint slot: no code system in the packaged index carries it, or its registered rows landed in no binding; "timed_out" means the request reached its time limit before this part was answered (diagnostics.timed_out is true); the question may hold data, so asking it again, alone or narrower, can answer it

cause.description: why this refusal fired, present only for reason=rate_coverage_gap (the structured door's same-named ProblemDetails extension); omitted on every other reason

category.title: Category
category.description: derived from reason, never independently settable: "entity_not_resolved", "entity_ambiguous", "entity_set_too_large", "entity_role_not_admitted", "variable_not_resolved", "role_not_resolved", "source_not_resolved", "source_ambiguous", "source_code_not_held", "source_code_ambiguous", "source_code_shares_variable", "unit_not_resolved", and "timed_out" are "unresolved" (the request could not be read into the graph); every other code is "absent" (the read request names a place holding nothing)

message.title: Message
message.description: the plain-language sentence for reason, naming the query terms it concerns where the reason has them (the indicator, place, or category wording), so a client can show a person the reason beside its code. Every no_data part the engine returns sets it. Clients must not parse it

nearest_real.title: Nearest Real
nearest_real.description: optional; up to two real, grounded specs found by relaxing one constraint at a time and re-confirming against the live graph. Each carries its own relaxation naming the definition part relaxed and the value(s) it dropped. Shaped by response_options and banded by confidence like any returned spec. Distinct from flagged_match (the elected variable itself) and alternate_match (a different variable). nearest_real varies the SAME variable's own constraints, never the variable.

gate.title: Gate
gate.description: optional; the failed quality gate's code from the platform registry, one of the three registry gate codes (no_member_has_data_at_place, no_member_asserts_bound_properties, only_alternate_has_data). The single home for the code regardless of which near-match field carries the Spec: present exactly when flagged_match or alternate_match is present, except a role_incompatible refusal before or during materialise whose flagged_match records the confirmed elected identity without a gate (role incompatibility prevents an availability verdict), a qualifier_not_bound refusal, whose flagged_match records the graph-confirmed elected spec without a gate because the qualifier guard refuses before an availability verdict exists, or a denominator_not_available refusal, whose flagged_match records the elected spec the form or denominator check refused. Absent on every other no_data outcome. At most one of flagged_match and alternate_match is present at a time.

flagged_match.description: optional; the elected variable's own Spec, present whenever gate fired and a groundable identity exists for the elected shape, or for a role_incompatible, qualifier_not_bound or denominator_not_available refusal that records its graph-confirmed identity without a gate: role incompatibility prevents an availability verdict, the qualifier guard refuses before one exists, and the denominator check refuses the series for its form, not its data. See gate for which check failed. available_at_place is False and confidence is low on gate=no_member_has_data_at_place; both stay at their not-assessed default (None) on gate=no_member_asserts_bound_properties, since there is no resolved place to be unavailable at. Absent on gate=only_alternate_has_data, where no groundable Spec for the elected shape exists; alternate_match carries the substitute the engine found instead. Distinct from nearest_real, up to two constraint-RELAXED specs that DO have data nearby. flagged_match is the elected variable itself, unavailable as the request asked for it.

alternate_match.description: optional; a categorically different, data-bearing variable the request did not elect, present exactly when gate == 'only_alternate_has_data'. elected_count still counts the variable the request actually asked for; alternate_match is the one substitute the engine found nearby with observations of its own. Distinct from flagged_match (the elected variable itself, present on the other two gates) and from nearest_real (up to two constraint-relaxed variants of the SAME variable). alternate_match always names a different variable.

elected_count.title: Elected Count
elected_count.description: optional; how many StatVars the request actually elected. Present whenever the elected shape's variable identity was graph-confirmed, whatever no_data reason or gate the outcome ultimately carries. None when the outcome stops short of a graph-confirmed identity altogether (variable_not_resolved, role_not_resolved, role_signature_incompatible, and binding_mismatch all resolve no StatVar to count). Counts the SAME variable as flagged_match whenever flagged_match is present. On gate=only_alternate_has_data, where flagged_match is absent, elected_count still counts the variable the request elected, distinct from alternate_match's different variable.

entity_terms.title: Entity Terms
entity_terms.description: the query entity text responsible for the outcome, in query order: every entity the engine could not resolve for entity_not_resolved, every ambiguous wording for entity_ambiguous, every resolved-but-unadmitted entity for entity_role_not_admitted, every name whose flow direction the query leaves untold for role_not_resolved, and every whole population the query directs to the other side of the flow for role_incompatible, which is empty when the refusal has another cause. Empty for every other no_data reason. This structured list is the client-facing source of those terms; rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.

ambiguous_entities.title: Ambiguous Entities
ambiguous_entities.description: every ambiguous wording responsible for an entity_ambiguous outcome, in query order, each paired with the graph candidates it could name. Empty for every other no_data reason. Invariant: every group's `text` equals some restatement.entities[i].text on the same part. Additive to entity_terms, which carries the same wordings as bare strings; rendered_sentence is unaffected by this field and quotes the same wordings and candidate names for people, but clients must not parse it.

source_terms.title: Source Terms
source_terms.description: the source wordings responsible for a source-resolution outcome, in query order: every included wording that matched no admitted source for source_not_resolved, every ambiguous wording for source_ambiguous, and the part's source_code for source_code_not_held, source_code_ambiguous and source_code_shares_variable. Empty for every other no_data reason. rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.

ambiguous_sources.title: Ambiguous Sources
ambiguous_sources.description: every ambiguous source wording responsible for a source_ambiguous outcome, in query order, each paired with the admitted sources it could name, and for source_code_ambiguous the part's source_code paired with the provenances holding it. Empty for every other no_data reason. A client posts the matching entry of options.

unit_alternatives.title: Unit Alternatives
unit_alternatives.description: the currencies a unit_not_resolved outcome offers, in the binder's order: the candidate ISO codes for an ambiguous currency name with no declared alias (XOF, XAF and CHF for 'francs'), or the role shapes for a role-relative currency phrase beside entities on two roles. Absent on every other outcome, and on a unit_not_resolved outcome the binder offers no candidates for

unbound_qualifiers.title: Unbound Qualifiers
unbound_qualifiers.description: the ResolvedQualifier entries responsible for a qualifier_not_bound outcome, in query order: every entry from flagged_match.resolved.trace.query_qualifiers whose disposition is not "bound" ("unbound": a named code row exists but no final binding covers it; "no_vocabulary": the text names no code at all), then, for a part naming or leaving out sources, each source it could not bind, an "unbound" entry under the source's label whose named holds the source's references. Empty for every other no_data reason. This structured list is the client-facing source of which terms went unrecognised, alongside each one's own disposition; rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.

denominator.description: the denominator the question named and the one the flagged match divides by, set on every denominator_not_available refusal the engine returns after electing a series; null for every other no_data reason. A client can offer the flagged match, or fetch its nearest_real level and the denominator asked and divide them

options.title: Options
options.description: one ready request per choice of an entity_ambiguous, source_ambiguous, source_code_ambiguous, role_not_resolved or unit_not_resolved refusal, in query then candidate order. An entity option pins the candidate on every row with the ambiguous wording and every entity that resolved to one node; named groups, sets read as members and other ambiguous wordings stay unpinned, so a second ambiguity refuses again with the first pick kept. A candidate that is a group's own node, asked for its members, posts the group's registry name with no dcid, and has no option when no registry name resolves to the group alone. A source option sets the candidate's ref on the ambiguous mention; a source-code option names the holding provenance as the part's only included source. A role option states a direction for every name the question left unstated, so that every axis the shape declares a role on and the part does not ask open holds a place, offered while that gives at most six readings. A unit option names one of unit_alternatives in place of the ambiguous currency words. An option whose part breaks the ParsedPart bounds, or states a direction its own wording contradicts, is left out. Empty for other reasons; when the part's inputs exceed the ParsedPart bounds; on a role_not_resolved refusal with more than six readings, with no reading that leaves a place on every such axis, whose readings were all read with none holding data, or that the shape refused before placing names; and on a unit_not_resolved refusal without unit_alternatives

NoData.title: NoData
NoData.description: Outcome when no grounded result can be returned.

asked.description: the denominator the question named, as the search read it from the bases the candidate series divide by; null when the question named none, or named one that no candidate series divides by

found.description: the denominator the flagged match divides by; null when it states none (a level such as an amount in US dollars, or a series whose name alone gives its base)

NoDataDenominator.title: NoDataDenominator
NoDataDenominator.description:
The denominators a denominator_not_available refusal compared: the one the question
named and the one its flagged match divides by -- NoData.denominator.

mentions.title: Mentions
mentions.description: the request's own words this option settles, in query order: the ambiguous entity wording, the ambiguous source wording, the part's source_code, the part's unit_text, or for role_not_resolved every name whose direction the option states

label.title: Label
label.description: the choice in words for a menu: the candidate's display name, prefixed 'Excluding' for a source the part excludes; for role_not_resolved the direction the option reads, such as 'France to Germany' or 'To Kenya and Uganda'; for a role currency the role's currency, such as "recipient's currency". Clients must not parse it

data_query.description: a one-part parsed input settling this choice only. Post it unchanged as the input of /api/search/resolve; its one part is a dataset_resubmit parsed entry's part. A second ambiguous wording refuses again. Whether data exists for it is not checked

entity_choice.title: Entity Choice
entity_choice.description: for an entity_ambiguous option, the index into NoData.ambiguous_entities of the group this option settles; null on every other option. Two groups can share one wording ('aid from Congo to Congo' asks 'Congo' for each end), so a client groups an entity menu by this index, never by mentions, and joins it to the sentence slot token with the same entity_choice

NoDataOption.title: NoDataOption
NoDataOption.description:
One answer to the choice a no_data refusal asks for: the words it settles, a label
for people, and the request that settles them. It is one entry of NoData.options.

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. Two parts marked separate that resolve to one reading carry the same spec_id and stay two parts. False, the default, is omitted

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order, and a candidates part's then closes with its assumptions clause. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

entity_refs.title: Entity Refs
entity_refs.description: the binding of each entity of `restatement`, one per restatement.entities row, in row order, so a client can tell which node a text such as 'G7' bound. A response field kept off `restatement`, which posts back unchanged. The binding is the one the answer reads: for a candidates part, the elected reading's; for a part folded into an earlier part's spec, its own. [] when `restatement` is null or names no entity

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

departures.title: Departures
departures.description: every way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, ordered by how much each changes the number: closest_match, measure_not_applied, operation_not_applied, breakdown_not_applied, entity_unavailable, year_unavailable, modelled_values, group_read_as_members, whole_total_read, whole_total_unpublished, direction_discarded, direction_inferred, scope_limited. [] when the answer is what was asked. A client that renders its own sentence reads them here; each one's text also closes the sentence that carries this part (see Departure.text). A warning on the same part reports run health and stays separate

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: every value the engine filled that the request did not ask for, in clause order. Declared defaults come first, in the order of the Spec's trace.slot_filters, then open roles, then the place scope. A declared default is a slot the request left open that its code system's or shape's declared default fixed, named by the bound code's full label. An open role is a flow role no request word asked for, read across every entity on it with data. It is either a role the role scope default filled (resolved.scope on that axis), whatever its member count, served as one series per member where the shape declares the role, or a role the heading states with no entity of its own ('from 164 providers', 'owed to all creditors'), served as the total over its members. A role the identity binds in entities or lists in open_roles, that one of the part's operations runs over ('top 5 donors'), or that the request's words asked every member of ('all donors'), is asked. The place scope is a request that named no place, read across every place with data. Every door fills assumptions. A definite part reads them from its Spec, a candidates part carries the items every list in CandidatesPart.reading_assumptions holds alike, text included, and no_data and unsupported parts carry []. A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts every slot bound, so its part states the items of the entry's assumptions echo that still hold (see ResubmitIdentityEntry.assumptions), and a candidates entry reads each reading with its candidate's echo (see ResubmitCandidate.assumptions). The sentence that carries this part closes with them as one segment='assumption' clause ('Assumed: official development assistance; every provider.'), after its departures. [] when the answer fills nothing

NoDataPart.title: NoDataPart
NoDataPart.description: Nothing could be returned for this part.

NodeRef.title: GraphNodeRef
NodeRef.description:
A graph reference. `label` is `null` when the target is not held, carries no `name`, or
carries only a `name` equal to its own dcid.

NodesRequest.title: GraphNodesRequest
NodesRequest.description:
`dcids`: 1 to `NODES_MAX_DCIDS` node dcids read as one batch, in one DCP-read
executor job. Each dcid matches the GET route's `{dcid}` path syntax and its 512-character
ceiling.

NodesResponse.title: NodesResponse
NodesResponse.description:
`nodes` is index-aligned with the request's `dcids`: a repeated dcid repeats its
entry. Each entry is the body `GET /api/graph/node/{dcid}` returns for that dcid, or a
`not_held` entry where that route answers 404.

NotHeldEntry.title: GraphNotHeldEntry
NotHeldEntry.description:
A batch entry for a dcid where `GET /api/graph/node/{dcid}` answers 404
`node_not_held`.

value.title: Value
value.description: the observed value; null when the graph reports a date with no value

ObservationPoint.title: ObservationPoint
ObservationPoint.description: One (date, value) pair from a resolved StatVar's observation series.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: the role tuple this series observes -- one entry for a standard single-role series (role='observationAbout'), two for a dev-finance bilateral series (role='origin' and role='destination')

axes.title: Axes
axes.description: one entry per constraint the StatVar declares with a resolved value, ordered by property dcid; empty for a StatVar with no constraints. A client names each property from the Spec's slots

points.title: Points
points.description: chronological observation points from the series' lead observation facet (see SpecObservations), plus the points of the same source's estimates continuing the series past the lead's last period when it has any -- the `modelled_values` departure marks those -- filtered to the spec's requested window when one exists; the full in-window series when SpecObservations.truncated is false, else at most the latest points (bounded by the server's preview-points setting and its per-series row limit)

total_obs.title: Total Obs
total_obs.description: this series' SELECTED facet's in-window point count (before truncation) -- a per-series figure alongside SpecObservations.total_obs's aggregate across every series. For a scope-defaulted bulk latest-only series (no requested window), this is the coverage probe's all-time obs_count for that entity's selected facet -- the in-window count too, since no window narrows it

source_refs.title: Source Refs
source_refs.description: provenance of the lead observation facet these points were read from (the facet selected for this series -- see SpecObservations)

facet.title: Facet
facet.description: this series' lead observation facet, per axis (provenance/measurementMethod/unit); the estimates continuing the series keep the lead's entry; sparse -- an axis the facet carries no value for is absent, never a null placeholder. provenance here always agrees with source_refs, since both derive from the same lead facet

conversion.description: what recipe and tables converted this series' points to the requested currency; absent on a series served in its native facet

ObservationSeries.title: ObservationSeries
ObservationSeries.description: One (stat_var, role tuple) pair's observation points, in chronological order.

recipe_id.title: Recipe Id
recipe_id.description: the ConversionRecipe.recipe_id that produced these points

table_provenance.description: the Provenance node both the exchange-rate and (when present) deflator tables loaded under

deflator_table_version.title: Deflator Table Version
deflator_table_version.description: the deflator table's own version; absent for a current-prices conversion

fallback_count.title: Fallback Count
fallback_count.description: rows whose deflator-role entity was substituted with the recipe's fallback entity

fallback_examples.title: Fallback Examples
fallback_examples.description: a capped, sorted sample of the substituted (entity, fallback_entity) pairs

projected_count.title: Projected Count
projected_count.description: rows whose rate/deflator term was sourced from a projected table row

projected_examples.title: Projected Examples
projected_examples.description: a capped, sorted sample of the affected 'entity@year' keys

ObservationSeriesConversion.title: ObservationSeriesConversion
ObservationSeriesConversion.description:
What produced a converted series' points: the recipe and table
versions, and the fallback/projected markers a caller reads off them.
Modelled on materialise.convert.ConversionRecord, whose own docstring
this field's members mirror. Omits ConversionRecord.native_currency:
a caller trusting or reproducing the number needs what recipe and
tables produced it, not what currency it started from -- facet.unit
already names the currency the points are actually in.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: machine-readable cause, equal to the accompanying Warning's code when one fires

message.title: Message
message.description: human-readable explanation, safe to render directly

pairs.title: Pairs
pairs.description: observations_preview_too_large only: the count that was too large

cap.title: Cap
cap.description: observations_preview_too_large only: the ceiling it exceeded

empty.title: Empty
empty.description: observations_no_points only: dispatched pairs that carried no data on their own facet

hard_failed.title: Hard Failed
hard_failed.description: observations_no_points (always 0) and observations_probe_failed: dispatched pairs whose fetch itself failed

facet_rejected.title: Facet Rejected
facet_rejected.description: observations_no_points (always 0) and observations_no_matching_source: dispatched pairs a bound facet_filter rejected

ObservationsOmission.title: ObservationsOmission
ObservationsOmission.description:
Why a SpecObservations payload carries no series, made unconditional:
every _fetch_observations call that reaches a "nothing to show" outcome
sets this field instead of leaving the whole payload absent, so a client
is never left guessing which of at least a dozen distinct causes
produced an empty preview.

reason is a warning code from search.engine.region.codes (see
ObservationsOmissionReason's own docstring for the closed vocabulary and
why it is duplicated here rather than imported) -- the SAME code the
accompanying Warning carries when one is also emitted, so a client reads
one vocabulary rather than two. Not every reason accompanies a Warning:
a genuinely uninteresting omission (nothing was ever there to probe)
carries no diagnostic Warning of its own, but always carries this field.

The converse also holds, and the pairing is not exhaustive: a reason
arriving as a bare Warning with `omitted` absent means partial coverage,
not absence -- a fetch that delivered some series would never set this
field, but can warn (`observations_probe_failed` on a partially hard-
failed fetch, and `observations_timed_out` on one some of whose pairs
crossed the deadline).

Whenever `omitted` is set, SpecObservations.series is `[]`, total_obs is
`0`, and truncated is `false`, so a client reading `series ?? []` and
ignoring `omitted` sees an ordinary empty result, with no schema_version
bump needed to stay compatible.

pairs/cap: populated only for reason=="observations_preview_too_large" --
the (stat_var, role_tuple) pair (or pair x elected-combination
dispatch-item, or distinct-stat_var) count that was compared against the
ceiling it crossed, and that ceiling itself. Lets a client render "this
selection has {pairs} series, above the {cap} the preview fetches"
without re-deriving either number.

dispatched: how many (stat_var, role_tuple) pairs this call actually
dispatched. Populated for reason=="observations_no_points",
"observations_probe_failed", "observations_no_matching_source", and
"observations_timed_out" -- every reason a dispatch actually happened
for; None for a reason reached before dispatch (e.g.
"observations_nothing_to_probe").

empty: dispatched pairs that carried no data on their own facet.
Populated only for reason=="observations_no_points".

hard_failed: dispatched pairs whose fetch itself failed. Populated for
reason=="observations_no_points" (always 0 there -- a nonzero count
means reason is "observations_probe_failed" instead) and for
"observations_probe_failed" itself (the nonzero count that produced
that reason); None elsewhere.

facet_rejected: dispatched pairs a bound facet_filter (or currency
conversion) rejected. Populated for reason=="observations_no_points"
(always 0 there -- a nonzero count means reason is
"observations_no_matching_source" instead) and for
"observations_no_matching_source" itself; None elsewhere.

Every field left None where the branch that produced this omission has
no meaningful count for it.

count.title: Count
count.description: how many distinct served members declare this value

OpenAxisValueCount.title: OpenAxisValueCount
OpenAxisValueCount.description:
One declared value on an open constraint axis and how many served members
declare it (see OpenConstraintAxisFact.values).

property.title: Property
property.description: the constraint property dcid this fact is about

varies.title: Varies
varies.description: False when every served member that declares a value for this axis declares the same one (including when none of them declare one at all, since declaring nothing is itself an agreeing value here, the same rule resolved.alternative_measures' own observed-partition read applies); True when they differ

value.description: the single value every served member that declares one for this axis agrees on; present only when varies is False and at least one member declares a value, absent when varies is True or every member declares nothing

distinct_count.title: Distinct Count
distinct_count.description: how many distinct declared values the served members actually exhibit for this axis, not counting a member that declares nothing. 0 when every member declares nothing, 1 when varies is False and value is set. Counted over the served members' own declarations, independent of this response's observation window: a query's applied when-slot narrows which observation points are returned, not which constraint values a member declares, so this count is never scoped to that window the way an observation-count field on this contract is

undeclared_count.title: Undeclared Count
undeclared_count.description: how many served members declare no value at all for this axis. A member whose arc names the axis but never resolved to a dcid counts here too, the same as a member that never asserted the axis at all

values.title: Values
values.description: every declared value with the number of served members declaring it, highest count first, then by dcid. Each served StatVar counts once, also after a merge of answers that serve it more than once, so the counts plus undeclared_count sum to the distinct served members. Labels as for value

OpenConstraintAxisFact.title: OpenConstraintAxisFact
OpenConstraintAxisFact.description:
One constraint axis the query left open, and what this Spec's own
served StatVar members exhibit on it (see ResolvedSpec.open_axis_facts):
whether they agree on a single declared value or differ, what that
agreed value is when one exists, how many distinct values the axis
actually served, and how many declare none at all.

verb.title: Verb
verb.description: what the question asks to compute: rank, aggregate, growth, share_of, explain, forecast, or report

phrase.title: Phrase
phrase.description: the query wording that asks for the operation, e.g. 'top 5 donors'; one line with no control characters or line separators, and not blank

over.title: Over
over.description: the axis the operation runs across (place, origin, destination, category, or year); null when the verb names none, as explain does. The part leaves this axis open, so its data covers every value the operation needs

target_year.title: Target Year
target_year.description: the year a forecast projects to, e.g. 2050 for 'forecast aid to Ethiopia to 2050'; set only on a forecast, a four-digit year up to 2200. The raw_text door sets it only to a year after the current one, and leaves it null when the question names none; a posted value is taken as given within the bound, whatever today's date. It is kept apart from the part's time_text, the years whose data the part fetches, and does not affect resolution

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description:
One computation the question asks for over a part's data, which search
does not perform: the part answers with the data the operation needs, and
the operation rides on the part for a client to perform or hand on.

operation_id.title: Operation Id
operation_id.description: `op_` plus the SHA-256 of the subject and its sorted member dcids, the origin catalogue build, and the rendering key. A repeat submission with the same identity joins the running operation and returns this id. Synchronous builds coalesce per API instance only.

retry_after_ms.title: Retry After Ms
retry_after_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait before the next poll. Present on the 202 submit response and on every pending or running poll. Absent on a done poll. It grows as the build runs, at a quarter of the time since the operation's current submission, from 1,500 to 8,000. The `Retry-After` response header carries the same value in whole seconds, rounded up.

OperationProgress.title: OperationProgress
OperationProgress.description:
`rows_written` against `estimate_rows`, read live off
`datasets.operation` at poll time (`datasets_api.operation_store
.Operation`). Present on a `pending`/`running` operation's own
envelope; omitted from the `202` submit envelope (nothing has run
yet) and from a terminal (`done`/`failed`) operation's own envelope,
whose outcome the sibling `manifest` field, or the poll route's own
`operation_failed` refusal, already carries in full.

OperationResource.title: OperationResource
OperationResource.description:
`GET /api/datasets/operations/{operation_id}`'s poll response. The
capability document reports `operation_envelope_active: true`, and this
is the shape the route returns for a known operation id in `pending`,
`running`, or `done` state. A `failed` operation raises the platform's
ordinary refusal path instead (`operation_failed`), and an unknown or
unauthorized-`done` id answers 404 `operation_not_found` -- neither
returns this shape.

`manifest` is set only once `operation.status == "done"`: the same
manifest a synchronous mint returns, read at poll time
(`datasets_api.doors.meta`'s operations route reuses `datasets_api
.doors.snapshot.read_snapshot_manifest` against the operation's own
stored `subject_id`/`content_version`). `error` models a `failed`
operation's outcome inline with this resource's own shape, but the
door never populates it: a `failed` operation raises the platform's
ordinary refusal path instead (`operation_failed`, a bare RFC 9457
body, the same pattern `operation_not_found` already uses on this
route -- see the registry's own `datasets.operations` mapping), so a
poll never reaches this model at all once the underlying operation
has failed. `error` stays declared for schema completeness -- this is
a contract-stable, immutable-`$id` shape -- but no code path fills it.

OptionsEnvelope.title: OptionsEnvelope
OptionsEnvelope.description:
`GET /api/datasets/{id}/options`'s response. It is the projection
of a materialising door's manifest onto the fields this route's callers
need (content_version, coverage, output_options, warnings, trace). The
route serves with no rendering (`doors.definition._serve_spec_options`),
so no reshape runs and `warnings` here excludes reshape-level warnings
such as `enrichment_unavailable`.

role.title: Role
role.description: the resolved entity role to enumerate candidates for (e.g. 'origin', 'destination', 'observationAbout' -- the vocabulary is derived per family, not frozen here). Deliberately a plain str, NEVER a Literal or enum: the target is checked only AFTER the posted identity resolves to StatVars, refusing option_target_invalid (422) for a role the resolved family does not carry. A Literal/enum would instead refuse an unrecognised role at the pydantic validation layer as request_invalid (400), before resolution ever runs -- do not tighten this to an enum.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: which candidate universe to enumerate for a role whose options are derived from the graph rather than a curated list; absent means 'peers'. 'peers' enumerates entities sharing the bound entity's own type; 'children' enumerates entities contained in it. Roles backed by a curated candidate list ignore this member, having only one universe to draw from. Naming a role alone cannot distinguish the two readings -- peers of a country and the regions within it are both 'options for observationAbout' -- and only the peers reading is recoverable from the identity, so without this member the contained-in reading is unreachable rather than merely unrequested.

OptionsFor.title: OptionsFor
OptionsFor.description:
Which resolved entity role the options door enumerates candidates for.

Wrapped in its own object (rather than a bare string field) so the wire
body reads `"for": {"role": "destination"}`, matching the contract's
envelope shape on both the request and the echoed response.

identity.description: the identity to resolve and enumerate candidate options for

for.description: which resolved entity role to enumerate candidate options for

include_coverage.title: Include Coverage
include_coverage.description: when true, the engine probes each returned option for observation coverage (e.g. 'Kenya — 205 obs') and populates SlotOption.coverage; false (the default) never fires the extra probe, so this is opt-in latency, not a hidden cost on the hot path. The only resolution option this door reads -- unlike /resolve's ResolveOptions, this door has no candidate cap or sentence concept, so it carries this one field directly rather than nesting a response_options object with members it would never use.

OptionsRequest.title: OptionsRequest
OptionsRequest.description:
Request body for the options door (POST /api/search/options): enumerate
the candidate set for one resolved entity role of a posted identity.

An identity block only. The door derives the identity's own StatVar
population server-side (engine.options.population.options_population)
rather than resolving a Spec through the resubmit path.

validate_by_name=False (with validate_by_alias=True, the pydantic default
pairing made explicit here): the published schema declares only the alias
`for`, and this model is otherwise extra="forbid", so a wire body must be
rejected for posting the internal Python attribute name `for_` instead --
accepting both would let a client bypass the declared schema through the
implementation-detail spelling. `for_` exists only because `for` is a
Python reserved word and cannot itself be an attribute name; every
constructor call (internal code, tests) builds this model through the
alias instead, e.g. ``OptionsRequest(identity=..., **{"for": OptionsFor(...)})``.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: contract schema version; exactly 1 for v1

diagnostics.description: run health, warnings, timing, build stamp

for.description: the role this response's options were enumerated for, echoed back from the request

OptionsResponse.title: OptionsResponse
OptionsResponse.description:
Response for POST /api/search/options: `{schema_version, diagnostics,
for, options}`. Carries no semantic status: the door either refuses
(through the same shared identity validation a dataset_resubmit identity
entry runs) or returns options -- possibly an empty
list -- with no definite/candidates/no_data three-way to report on top.

Omits graph_revision: no revision concept exists anywhere in src/ --
nothing tracks the graph the way engine_build tracks the code build -- so
stamping one here would assert a graph fact this deployment cannot back.
Left out deliberately rather than filled with something untrue.

items.title: Items
items.description: candidate values, deterministically ordered; a dcid that failed to resolve a label is omitted rather than fabricated

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: true when items was capped before every candidate could be checked

OptionsSet.title: OptionsSet
OptionsSet.description:
The enumerated candidate set an options-door request returns.

Items reuse SlotOption for shape parity with slot_options/entity_options
({value, coverage}) rather than a simpler {ref, label, obs_count} shape --
the richer coverage form is what the engine already serves. An
empty list is itself a valid result (e.g. the current recipient's
variable truly has no other recipient with data), not an error.

Carries no graph_revision -- see OptionsResponse's docstring for why.

built_from.description: the build of each table the response read

OtherNode.title: OtherNode
OtherNode.description: A node no other kind fits. `types` and `description` carry what the graph holds.

long_layout_defaults.title: Long Layout Defaults
long_layout_defaults.description: the enrichment tokens a long-layout download writes with no columns option, in column order: every role's {role}_label, and {role}_kind for every role on a flow axis, the party's kind in words: official or private on the provider or creditor side, country or organisation on the recipient or debtor side, total, whole total (a total that holds every party of its group in that row's dataset and year) or unallocated. Naming one in columns gives the same column once

long_layout_totals.title: Long Layout Totals
long_layout_totals.description: the roles whose total rows ({role}_kind is total or whole total) a long-layout CSV or XLSX download keeps out of its main table. A private party stays in it. A role is listed when the definition binds it to several entities one of which the code index declares a total, or leaves it open and the code index lists a total on its axis in a dataset the definition read (any dataset, when the read selected none). A role bound to several parties holds no total row and is not listed. A bundle's CSV writes those rows to a second data file, data/<name>-totals.csv; an XLSX writes them on a second sheet, totals. A bare CSV has no README and drops them, so this list names the roles whose totals it drops. Parquet, a pivot and the frame layout keep every row. Empty when no role can hold a total row

OutputOptionsModel.title: OutputOptionsModel
OutputOptionsModel.description:
The reshape options this frame supports, joined from its stored
`materialise.profile.OutputProfile` and the current capability
document.

text.title: Text
text.description: the entity's text as the caller identified it: the request's own words for it, which name resolution reads and a rendered sentence quotes

name.title: Name
name.description: the entity's name, when its words (`text`) could name more than one entity and no `dcid` pins it: the row's identity, which keys its role and members within the part. Name resolution reads `text` with `name` beside it, as the raw-text door reads a query's words beside the name extraction gave them, so two rows whose words are alike stay two entities. Words that differ from `name` only in case read as `name`, and one `name` posted with two texts that differ beyond case in a part refuses `request_invalid`. Without it, `text` is the identity; a `name` equal to `text` is the field left out, and a `name` beside a `dcid` is invalid. A row no dcid pins whose identity, its `name` or else its `text`, is a dcid another row of the part pins refuses `request_invalid` at the row

role_text.title: Role Text
role_text.description: the caller's free-form role hint for this entity, when available; recognised words (case-insensitive) are 'from'/'to' and synonyms such as donor/provider/funder/source/creditor/lender/exporter for the 'from' side, recipient/beneficiary/debtor/borrower/importer for the 'to' side -- unrecognised text warns role_text_not_recognised and the entity is treated as undirected

dcid.title: Dcid
dcid.description: an optional caller-pinned dcid for this entity, naming exactly which graph node `text` refers to -- the door a client with a candidate's dcid in hand (e.g. from NoData.ambiguous_entities) posts through, instead of relying on name resolution to disambiguate `text` on its own. When present, this entity's name resolution is skipped: the pinned dcid seeds the entry's pre_resolved map directly, still confirmed against the graph. An unconfirmable dcid (absent from the graph, or present but type-less) refuses invalid_role_ref (422). `text` stays required and is not re-derived from the dcid; it is still what a rendered sentence and any further restatement echo back. The dcid is the row's identity, so rows pinning one dcid under different texts are one entity, whose words are the first row's. A row no dcid pins whose `name`, or else `text`, is this dcid refuses request_invalid at that row.

members.title: Members
members.description: true asks for the members of the set `text` names, each as its own series: the countries of a continent or UN subregion, or the members of a group. It has no effect on a single place. Text whose wording names members, such as 'EU member states', reads as true without the flag. With a pinned `dcid` it is honoured for a continent or subregion that the membership policy holds or omits, whatever the node's graph type, and refuses request_invalid for a group's own node, whose members a pin cannot supply. One part names a set once: the same entity posted with both values refuses request_invalid

ParsedEntity.title: ParsedEntity
ParsedEntity.description: One entity mentioned in a parsed part, with an optional caller-supplied role hint.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: one entry per variable ask; conjunctions pre-split by the caller. Parts that are byte-identical across every field collapse to one before resolution, so the response's own parts list can hold fewer entries than this list.

raw_query.title: Raw Query
raw_query.description: original query text, for echo only; does not affect resolution

ParsedInput.title: ParsedInput
ParsedInput.description:
Pre-parsed input: one or more variable parts supplied directly by the caller,
skipping natural-language extraction.

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: the variable's text as the caller identified it

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: entities associated with this part's variable, when available; null, omitted, or an empty list all mean no entity was named for this part, resolving the variable globally/entity-less -- the same meaning a raw_text query with no extracted place carries

time_text.title: Time Text
time_text.description: this part's time expression, when available; recognised forms include a bare four-digit year, 'YYYY to YYYY' or 'YYYY-YYYY', 'from YYYY to YYYY', 'between YYYY and YYYY', a latest end as in 'between YYYY and the latest' or 'YYYY to latest', 'since YYYY', 'latest', 'latest year available', 'most recent', and 'last N years'. Anything else resolves dateless with a time_text_not_parsed warning, whose message lists every form

unit_text.title: Unit Text
unit_text.description: this part's requested unit or measurement basis, when available; recognised phrasing names a currency (ISO 4217 code or curated name/alias), a price basis (current or constant prices), and/or a base year (e.g. '2015 US dollars', 'constant prices, 2015 base year'). A phrase this text failed to parse cleanly resolves no_data with unit_not_resolved; a phrase the request grammar cannot express at all resolves unsupported with unit_request_unsupported. A phrase the grammar CAN express is checked against this deployment's own unit data: a currency/prices/base_year combination no unit this deployment carries expresses at all resolves unsupported with facet_binding_unsupported; one this deployment can express but that matches no candidate observation resolves no_data with facet_not_available; a match resolves definite, applying the completed request to the resolved spec's identity and carrying request_basis on resolved.facets.unit

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: the data sources this part names or excludes, in query order. Empty, the part answers from the sources the engine elects. A restatement echoes each mention with the reference it resolved to

source_text.title: Source Text
source_text.description: deprecated: post `sources` instead. Read as one included mention with this text, appended to `sources`

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: deprecated: post `sources` instead. Read as one included mention with this ref, appended to `sources`. The served request schema lists the code index's declared datasets under this field, each with its label, description and opt-in flag

source_code.title: Source Code
source_code.description: a publisher's own series code for this part's variable, such as the World Bank's DT.TDS.DEGG.CD, when the user or a skill gives one. Compared upper-cased, it names the variables the publisher gives that code, and the part answers from them in place of matching variable_text; variable_text, entities and open_roles still choose among them. A code is never a constraint and narrows nothing else. A code whose variables cannot answer the part, because no source search serves holds it, the part's sources leave out every source holding it, or its variables cannot answer the part as asked, resolves no_data with source_code_not_held, its message naming the cause; a code two of the part's sources hold resolves no_data with source_code_ambiguous until `sources` names one; a code whose variable another code of its source also names resolves no_data with source_code_shares_variable, naming those codes

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

open_roles.title: Open Roles
open_roles.description: the roles this part asks for member by member, at most one word per flow axis, e.g. ['creditor'] for 'debt service paid to each creditor'. Each is a role_text word: creditor, donor, recipient, debtor, origin, destination, or a synonym. Where the answer's family declares the role, the answer holds one series per member of it and its identity states the axis in open_roles; a role named in neither entities nor open_roles reads as the total over that role. An unrecognised word, or a role one of this part's entities binds through role_text, refuses request_invalid. An operation whose over is origin or destination opens that axis too

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them, as in 'health ODA versus education ODA': it answers as its own part and never folds into another part of the same shape (binding_folded). False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer. Two parts marked separate that resolve to one reading carry the same spec_id and stay two parts

ParsedPart.title: ParsedPart
ParsedPart.description: One variable ask within a parsed request, with its own entities, time, unit, and source.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: the role properties a node of these types can fill, by the role ranges the graph declares (rangeIncludes and its subClassOf closure); null when that read failed

ProvenanceRef.title: ProvenanceRef
ProvenanceRef.description:
A provenance on the wire: its dcid and label, the source behind it, the
Data Commons its data comes from, and the route of its document, which
follows from the dcid. `label`, `source` and `data_commons` come from the
origin catalogue's provenance table. A provenance the table does not list
carries its graph label and neither `source` nor `data_commons`, and is
omitted when the graph has no label for it.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: contract schema version; exactly 1 for v1

spec_id.title: Spec Id
spec_id.description: the derived frame's own op-spec hash id, ops_-prefixed

content_version.title: Content Version
content_version.description: the derived frame's own toolkit content version, ocv_-prefixed

role_keys.title: Role Keys
role_keys.description: `dfo_frame_grammar.Frame.build`'s own `role_keys` argument; empty is a valid subject-only frame with no role columns, `build_frame` accepts it, so no minimum is imposed here. Bounded at 16 entries, each at most 1024 characters, a schema fact rather than a deployment ceiling -- see this module's own docstring

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: `dfo_frame_grammar.Frame.build`'s own `rows` argument; empty is a valid frame (an analysis verb whose filter matches nothing produces exactly this), `build_frame` accepts it, so no minimum is imposed here. Each row is bounded at 22 keys; the outer list is bounded at 1000000 rows, a fixed schema backstop, well above doors.publish's own fixed PUBLISH_MAX_ROWS that actually governs `len(rows)` at publish time -- see this module's own docstring for why the two are not the same kind of cap. A cell is a scalar, or under `unit` alone a mapping of scalars bounded at 3 entries or a composed unit, `numerator` over `denominator`, each a unit ref, a mapping of scalars, or `{stat_var}` -- see this module's own docstring for the shapes refused at parse time

input_content_versions.title: Input Content Versions
input_content_versions.description: every input frame's own frame-grammar content_version this derived frame was computed from. Bounded at 256 entries, a schema fact rather than a deployment ceiling -- see this module's own docstring

recipe.description: the recipe that produced this frame. The door stores it beside the version, outside the body a republish is compared on, so a republish may add one to a frame published without it and may omit one the frame already holds

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: the frame's step records, one per operation that computed it, in order, in the shape of dfo-spec-kit's step schema. `op` is any operation name. At most 62 steps and 65536 bytes of canonical JSON; step ids are distinct, an input that names a step names an earlier one, and only a `retrieve` step's `input` names a version, which at least one does. The versions `retrieve` steps name are the frame's root inputs, which `input_content_versions`, the immediate input frames, need not list. Absent when the publish carries none

created.title: Created
created.description: true when this call newly recorded the version row; false when an identical publish of this exact pair had already been recorded (the idempotent replay path)

normalized_query.title: Normalized Query

extract_skipped.title: Extract Skipped
extract_skipped.description: true when the extraction step was skipped for this request

QueryEcho.title: QueryEcho

RawTextInput.title: RawTextInput
RawTextInput.description: Natural-language query input. The engine extracts, resolves, and grounds it.

normal_form_hash.title: Normal Form Hash
normal_form_hash.description: hash of the recipe's normal form, in which every derived input is replaced by its own recipe, every root by its dataset spec_id and rendering, and every literal a rolling overlay governs is dropped. Two frames replayed from one recipe on different data share it

replay_key.title: Replay Key
replay_key.description: hash of the normal form hash, the root dataset pairs, and the execution identity. It names the one frame replayed from them

execution_identity.title: Execution Identity
execution_identity.description: the engine, grammar, and reduction versions that ran the recipe

tree.title: Tree
tree.description: the op-spec tree, opaque here; analysis-mcp owns its shape

roots.title: Roots
roots.description: how each root dataset was minted, opaque here; analysis-mcp owns its shape

anchor.description: the rolling anchor, or null for a recipe with no rolling period

period.title: Period

rule.title: Rule

RecipeAnchor.description: The period a rolling recipe's `latest` resolved to, and the series it left out.

root.title: Root
root.description: index of the population the series belongs to, in the order of the recipe's populations: one per root dataset

coordinates.description: the series' dimension values, column name to value. Holds `stat_var` or at least one entity-role column

label.title: Label
label.description: the series' display name. Optional: a reader of the recipe resolves the name from `coordinates` when it is absent

RecipeLeftOutSeries.title: RecipeLeftOutSeries
RecipeLeftOutSeries.description:
One series a rolling anchor left out: it holds no row at the anchor period.

`coordinates` must name the series, since a reader labels it from them: they hold
`stat_var`, or at least one entity-role column, which is any column other than the frame
grammar's fixed columns (`stat_var`, `time_period`, `value`, `unit`, `status`) and its
facet identity columns (`measurementMethod`, `provenance`). Empty coordinates, and
coordinates of only those other columns, are refused.

created.title: Created
created.description: true when this call stored the recipe; false when the frame already held a recipe with the same normal_form_hash and replay_key

RegisterRequest.description:
`POST /api/datasets/register`'s body: one canonical `definition`.
`unsupported_schema_version` (the top-level `schema_version` field's own
refusal) and any other shape failure surface through the platform's
generic `RequestValidationError` handling.

stat_var.description: the StatVar this measure reads, labelled with its graph name, or its dcid when it has none

RelatedMeasure.title: RelatedMeasure
RelatedMeasure.description:
One other StatVar from the StatVarGroup this Spec's one StatVar belongs to (see
ResolvedSpec.related_measures), with data at the Spec's places.

`definition` is minted from the member's own five-tuple and constraint values, with this
Spec's entities and requested window and no facets, since a unit or source this Spec
pins belongs to its own measure. Post `definition` back as `identity` on a
dataset_resubmit identity entry to switch onto this measure.

property_dcid.title: Property Dcid
property_dcid.description: the constraint property dcid the relaxed slot carried, when one exists

dropped_value_dcids.title: Dropped Value Dcids
dropped_value_dcids.description: the taxonomy member dcid(s) the relaxed binding dropped

Relaxation.title: Relaxation
Relaxation.description:
Which definition part a nearest_real suggestion relaxed to find data.

Captured at the point a constraint binding is dropped and the resulting,
widened request is re-confirmed against the live graph (see
NearestRealSpec). Names the definition part relaxed (axis + the
constraint property it carried) and the value(s) it dropped.

member_types.description: every component type this release's catalogue defines

constraint_ids.title: Constraint Ids
constraint_ids.description: every constraint id this release's registry enforces

retry_modes.title: Retry Modes
retry_modes.description: `retry_modes` is the headline mode per code, and the per-response `retryable` boolean is the authoritative value for every code. `schema_invalid` and `frame_unavailable` vary by cause, and `request_invalid` is always false although its headline mode is `correct_and_retry`.

envelope_schema.title: Envelope Schema
envelope_schema.description: the envelope JSON Schema this release's assembler validates a minted envelope against; every create/revise/read body's `resolved_payload` conforms to it

component_schemas.title: Component Schemas
component_schemas.description: each member type's own component JSON Schema, keyed by member type. `envelope_schema`'s `component` field `$ref`s these schemas by their own `$id`, which otherwise resolves nowhere, so a client validating `resolved_payload` resolves those `$ref`s against this map

intent_schemas_tolerant.title: Intent Schemas Tolerant
intent_schemas_tolerant.description: each member type's own tolerant intent schema

minimal_intents.title: Minimal Intents
minimal_intents.description: each member type's own minimal legal intent

ReleaseDocumentResponse.description:
`GET /api/presentation/release`'s body. It carries the pinned
catalogue release's own identity and the vocabulary a client needs
to mount tools without a second, out-of-band fetch of the catalogue
bundle.

ReleaseModel.title: ReleaseModel
ReleaseModel.description: One release of a source's DFO pipeline.

RenderBody.title: RenderBody
RenderBody.description: The frame to draw the revision on.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: contract schema version; exactly 1 for v1. Required on every response.

query_echo.description: what the response was understood to be answering

diagnostics.description: run health, warnings, timing, build stamp

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: discriminator for a response that resolved the question into data

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: one entry per variable asked, in query order

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: the envelope-level confirmation sentence describing the whole query, composed across every part's own sentence in query order. When every contributing part is definite, their headings join into one sentence. A qualifier axis (where, when, or source, each a wire value of axis, plus origin, identified by role=='origin' instead since SentenceAxis has no 'origin' member) whose bound value agrees across every contributing part is stated once after the joined phrases, a possessive lead every part shares opens the sentence once, and the byline follows once. A qualifier that differs stays inline in each part's own phrase. The response falls back to one sentence per part, each part's own text left exactly as that part rendered it, when a part is still resolving, when the parts' bylines differ, or when a differing qualifier's connective opens with a comma (a period range). A part still resolving contributes up to three tokens of its own: an optional prefix text token, its own variable_text as an editable slot, and a text token stating the outcome. A lone part that is not definite composes to exactly that part's own sentence. After the headings and bylines, each part's departures follow in part order as segment='departure' tokens carrying that part's part_index. This is the one sentence that writes out a definite part's departures. The parts' assumptions close the sentence as segment='assumption' tokens. A joined sentence takes one clause, each item carrying the part_index of its part and an item two parts share carrying none. A sentence written part by part takes each part's own clause after its departures. There, a part whose sentence and clause both repeat an earlier part's is stated once with it, that sentence and clause carrying no part_index, followed by each part's own departures, and a part whose clause differs keeps its own sentence. On a mixed resolution with at least one definite part, the sentence opens 'Answered N of M parts.', where N counts the definite parts, folded ones included, and M is len(parts).

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present under the same condition; null or omitted otherwise. Composed the same way rendered_sentence is, from every part's own sentence_plan -- see SentenceToken.part_index for how a client recovers which parts[i] each variable phrase and attached qualifier belongs to, and which tokens are shared skeleton (an inter-phrase connective, a hoisted shared qualifier, the terminal '.', or the shared ' ' the per-part fallback puts between two sentences) rather than any one part's own. On a mixed resolution with at least one definite part, the plan opens with two segment='coverage' tokens carrying no part_index, 'Answered N of M parts.' and ' '. A mixed resolution with no definite part has no opener.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: every skill named by any Spec.resolved.skills across this response's parts, keyed by id -- each id any Spec carries is a key here, and each key's front matter is carried once regardless of how many Specs name it. Present under response_options.include_skills; null when the option is off, {} when it is on and no Spec matched anything.

status.title: Status
status.description: the parts' shared status when every part agrees, or 'mixed' when two or more parts differ; derived from parts, never independently settable

Resolution.title: Resolution
Resolution.description:
A resolve response that resolved the question into data: one part per
variable asked, in query order, each a complete outcome carrying its own
status and payload.

A single-variable query is one part, so `status` reads that one part's
status directly. A query in which extraction found no variable is also
one part, whose `variable_text` is the whole query text.

`status` below is a computed field that rides in every serialised
response body without being a settable input, so this class stays a
plain `BaseModel`, which allows unknown fields. `StrictModel` forbids them,
which would make `Resolution.model_validate` reject its own `model_dump()`
output, breaking every round-trip a client or this codebase does on a
fetched response body. A posted `status` is ignored and recomputed.

Usage::

    resp = RESOLVE_RESPONSE_ADAPTER.validate_python(obj)
    if resp.kind == "resolution":
        resp.status          # "definite" | "candidates" | "no_data" | "unsupported" | "mixed"
        resp.parts[0].status  # this part's own status

slot_filters.title: Slot Filters
slot_filters.description: each applied bind decision, slot by slot

query_qualifiers.title: Query Qualifiers
query_qualifiers.description: each narrowing term the request's text named, and what became of it (see ResolvedQualifier). Defaulted empty: a dataset_resubmit identity entry carries no query text to re-derive this from, and every hand-built fixture and same-shape merge that predates this field still validates.

requested_window.title: Requested Window
requested_window.description: the date window originally requested (query intent), independent of coverage narrowing; None when no date was requested. The literal "latest" means the query explicitly asked for the most-recent/current value -- distinct from None (no date signal at all), since a resubmit of a "latest" spec must re-resolve to whatever year is CURRENTLY latest, not pin to the year this response happened to resolve. spec_id is anchored on this value, not on the served window, so identity stays stable across a resubmit even when coverage narrows the dates. Preserve the returned Spec.definition.identity when resubmitting; if editing it, carry this value at ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity.requested_window to keep that stability.

capability_version.title: Capability Version
capability_version.description: the deployment capability version that produced this Spec, shared verbatim with GET /api/search/capabilities and every problem-details body's own capability_version. None only in hand-built fixtures that predate this field; every engine-produced Spec populates it.

default_reading.description: what the default price-basis reading did before bind (see TraceDefaultReading); None when no bind ran for this Spec, as on a resubmit, or in hand-built fixtures that predate this field

stated_form.title: Stated Form
stated_form.description: the normalised form the quantity read found in the question when no wording pattern named one ("debt to GDP" asks for a rate), and which the answer was then checked against; None when a wording pattern named the form, when the question asks for none, and when no bind ran for this Spec

conversion.description: always absent: conversion is recorded per series in resolved.observations.series[].conversion (see TraceConversion)

ResolutionTrace.title: ResolutionTrace
ResolutionTrace.description: Consolidated record of how the query was understood.

include_option_coverage.title: Include Option Coverage
include_option_coverage.description: when true, the engine probes each top-level interpretation and candidate Spec's slot_options for observation coverage (e.g. 'Kenya — 205 obs') and populates SlotOption.coverage; false/absent (the default) never fires the extra probes, so this is opt-in latency, not a hidden cost on the hot path. Delivery differs by transport, for every input kind: over SSE (Accept: text/event-stream), coverage arrives via trailing slot_options/entity_options events emitted after the response event, and the response event's own Spec.resolved.slot_options / entity_options stay coverage=null; on the buffered JSON body, coverage is embedded directly in the returned Spec. Spec.resolved.facet_options is computed whether or not this is set; over SSE with this set, it arrives in trailing facet_options events instead of the response event.

include_observations.title: Include Observations
include_observations.description: when true (the default is false -- absent also means false), the engine populates Spec.resolved.observations with the resolved answer's observation values: the full series when small enough, otherwise a bounded latest-points preview. This per-spec fetch runs only after the engine commits to a definite spec, including a promoted candidate; a multi-candidate response keeps per-candidate metadata and coverage without fetching observations. Delivery mirrors include_option_coverage's transport split: over SSE, observations arrive via a trailing observations event emitted after the response event, and the response event's own Spec.resolved.observations stays null or omitted; on the buffered JSON body, observations are embedded directly in the returned Spec.

include_skills.title: Include Skills
include_skills.description: when true (the default is false -- absent also means false), the engine matches every resolved Spec's bound graph nodes (its shape's structural anchors and the dcids its bound constraint slots name) and its selected provenance (facets.provenance.ref, when one provenance serves every series) against the shared skills index and populates Spec.resolved.skills with the matching skill ids: skills matched through a graph node first, nearest-attachment-first, then skills matched only through the provenance, by id; [] when nothing matched. The response's own skills map then carries every named skill's front matter once, keyed by id. When the shared skills index has not yet built a first snapshot, the response carries the skills_index_unavailable diagnostics warning instead and no Spec gets a populated skills field; when a snapshot is available but its own build may have left out a published skill or served one excluded or understated (a read stopped at a budget or bound, the build's content budget ran out before a skill's turn, or a build step failed), the response instead carries the skills_index_incomplete diagnostics warning alongside whatever matches it did serve; a part with no resolved spec (no_data, unsupported) carries the part-scoped skills_not_matchable warning, since it binds no graph nodes to match against.

ResolveOptions.title: ResolveOptions
ResolveOptions.description: Optional resolution parameters the caller may supply.

ResolveResult.title: GraphResolveResult
ResolveResult.description:
One text's outcome. `input` echoes the text; fields a status does not use are `null`.

- `resolved`: `entity`, `matched` and `reading`. A group or region adds `projection`,
  `member_count` and `members`: the list route's link, or the members inline (at most
  256) when the request expanded them. The three are `null` for a region the membership
