  policy does not hold. `near_matches` lists up to 3 other places or organisations of the
  requested kinds that share the name ("Georgia" resolves to the country, with the US
  state `geoId/13` here), else `null`. When `kinds` removed the first match, a node of a
  requested kind sharing the name resolves in its place and `near_matches` lists the
  removed match ("Georgia" with `kinds: ["place_other"]` resolves to `geoId/13`, with
  the country here).
- `ambiguous`: `candidates`, in the resolver's order. When `kinds` removed the first
  match and up to 3 nodes of a requested kind share the name, `near_matches` lists the
  removed match, else `null`.
- `not_found`: `near_matches`, hints for a person; a program should pick none by id.
- `not_held`: `entity`, the id the resolver named, which does not open on the node route.

`reading` is `members` when the text names a group's members ("EU countries"), else
`entity`.

label.title: Label
label.description: plain-language display name

role.title: Role
role.description: the role key this entity plays; observationAbout, origin, or destination

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: the engine's confidence in this entity resolution; None when not assessed -- no entity-resolution confidence signal exists yet, so this ships None on every entity today

ResolvedEntity.title: ResolvedEntity
ResolvedEntity.description:
One resolved entity on the wire, under `resolved.entities`: the flat
projection of the engine's own `Entity` -- `ref`/`entity_type` collapse from
a `GraphRef` to a bare dcid/label pair, and `role` collapses from the
engine's richer role model to the role-key string it already derives from
(the identity core's own vocabulary, so this never adds a second mapping).

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: 'bound' when this axis was constrained by the request, 'declared_default' when an unbound axis was completed from a declared deployment policy, 'fallback' when neither applies and the deployment policy supplied the value: facets holding a point in the requested years first, then DFO's facets for a variable both DFO and base Data Commons hold, then the most places or role tuples covered there, then the most requested years the span covers, then most observations, then the latest observation, then a deterministic tie-break

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the axis's resolved dcid, present when one distinct value served every carried series; absent when selection is 'per_series'

label.title: Label
label.description: best-effort display label for ref; present only alongside ref

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: unit axis only, alongside ref: the ISO 4217 code of the currency ref is denominated in, from the graph's currency units (CurrencyUSD, USDollar and the base Data Commons Currency members such as INR); absent when ref is no currency. The sentence reads it: US dollars go to the byline's unit token, any other currency stays in the heading

source.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the organisation behind the provenance, from the origin catalogue

data_commons.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the Data Commons the provenance's data comes from

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the Graph API route of the provenance's document, GET /api/graph/documentation/{dcid}

account.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: whose account of a flow the provenance gives, when ref is a dataset the code index declares; 'provider' when it reports flows as their providers record them

selection.title: Selection
selection.description: 'per_series' when the carried series select different values on this axis; present in place of ref/label, never alongside them

request_basis.title: Request Basis
request_basis.description: per-member basis (currency/prices/base_year) for a unit axis bound through the request form; present only on the unit axis, alongside either ref/label or selection

ResolvedFacet.title: ResolvedFacet
ResolvedFacet.description:
One facet axis's resolved value on a Spec (see ResolvedSpec.facets):
which value backed the answer's observations, and why.

basis is always present. ref/label are present when one distinct value
served every carried series; selection carries "per_series" in their
place when the carried series select different values on this axis --
never alongside ref/label. request_basis joins either shape, present
only on the unit axis, only when unit was bound through the request form
(currency/prices/base_year), one basis value per member the request
named.

Fields are flat and optional, validated by a model validator, rather
than a discriminated ref/selection union. basis and request_basis are
shared by both the single-ref and per-series shapes, so a union would
duplicate them across arms for a mechanical gain (moving the
ref/selection XOR to the type level) without expressing the
request_basis-only-on-unit constraint, since that constraint is about
which AXIS a ResolvedFacet lives under (see ResolvedSpec.facets), not
its ref/selection shape. This is also response-only data, never
deserialized from untrusted client bytes, so a runtime validator is
the right tool for catching an illegal engine-side construction.

refs.title: Refs
refs.description: the bound graph objects (empty for unbound)

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: whether the bind call's own election produced this value, a code row recognised in the query's own text forced it, or the measure-family election forced it on an axis the binder left open

ResolvedFilter.title: ResolvedFilter
ResolvedFilter.description: One applied bind decision, slot by slot.

text.title: Text
text.description: verbatim span of the source text that named the term: variable_text, query_text, or a dropped qualifier phrase

named.title: Named
named.description: every code row the span names in the packaged index, any code system, and every measure value it names that the answer does not carry; empty when none did

slot.title: Slot
slot.description: property dcid of the slot_filters entry whose binding consumed this term, or, on an unbound value the answer's shape has a slot for but leaves unmet, that slot's property; None otherwise

disposition.title: Disposition
disposition.description: "bound" when a final binding covers a named row (or a descendant of one); "unbound" when a code row was named but no binding covers it, or a measure value was named that the answer does not carry; "no_vocabulary" when the term names neither

start.title: Start
start.description: character offset where the term starts in the variable phrase

end.title: End
end.description: character offset where the term ends in the variable phrase

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: what read the term: a code label or synonym, the bind model, "uncovered" for words no reader covers on the elected shape, unbound beside a recognised code or naming a measure value the answer does not carry, and no_vocabulary beside none when the binder rated them as not stated by its series, "unavailable" for a code no table holds, "unsupported" for a distinction no binding expresses

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: how the term's codes combine with another term's on one code system: a union of both, or a refinement to the narrower

selected.title: Selected
selected.description: the codes the term asked for before the combination simplified them

ResolvedQualifier.title: ResolvedQualifier
ResolvedQualifier.description:
One narrowing term the request's text named, and what became of it.

The term's text can come from the variable phrase, from the verbatim
`query_text`, or from an admitted qualifier tie (see
`_resolve_query_qualifiers`). `text` is the verbatim span of whichever
source named it. `named` is every code row -- any system -- that span
names in the packaged index, and every measure value it names that the
answer does not carry (a dcid of the index's measure values, such as
`amountMobilised`);
empty when the text names neither (a `no_vocabulary` term). `slot`
is the constraint property dcid of the `slot_filters` entry whose
binding consumed the term, or, on an `"unbound"` value the answer's shape
has a slot for but leaves unmet, that slot's property; `None` otherwise.
`disposition` is
`"bound"` when some final binding on a named row's code system covers
it (that row or a descendant), `"unbound"` when a code row was named but
no binding covers it or a measure value was named that the answer does not
carry, and `"no_vocabulary"` when the term names neither: an LLM-reported
phrase (`bind`'s own `unplaced` output) that no taxonomy in this
deployment's index can express, an exclusion or comparison phrase
(`"unsupported"`), or words beside no code the binder rated as not stated
on the elected shape (`"uncovered"`).

`start` and `end` locate the term in the part's variable phrase. `evidence` says what
read it, and `None` means a code's label or synonym matched the term as the query
spelled it, the reading every recognised span records:

- `"label"` and `"synonym"` name a match on a code's label or synonym; no record sets
  them, since a recognised span records `None`.
- `"model"` marks a phrase the bind model read through a code it chose from the
  phrase's candidate menu, a lexical hit of the menu or a descendant of one
  (`phase_rank_bind._model_records`); `named` holds the chosen codes.
- `"uncovered"` marks words no reader covers on the elected shape
  (`phase_rank_bind._coverage_records`). Beside a recognised code they are recorded
  `"unbound"` with that code's rows as `named`. On a shape the measure index describes,
  a word that every name of a measure value's reading holds names that value when no
  span names it and the answer does not carry it, and its record adds the value to
  `named`. Beside no code such a word is recorded `"unbound"` naming the value, whatever
  the binder rates it; "mobilised" names `amountMobilised` on an amount series. Other
  words beside no code are recorded `"no_vocabulary"` with `named` empty when the
  binder rates them below `SearchSettings.stated_word_bar` as not stated by the shape's
  series; a word it rates at the bar or above, or leaves unrated, reads as stated.
- `"unavailable"` marks a code term the elected shape cannot apply: one naming only
  codes no shape can bind, or, on a part naming a dataset, one no row of that dataset
  holds (`phase_rank_bind._unavailable_qualifiers`), recorded `"unbound"`.
- `"unsupported"` marks an exclusion or comparison phrase no binding expresses
  (`phase_rank_bind._unsupported_records`), recorded `"no_vocabulary"`.

`operation` and `selected` describe how the term's codes combine with
another term's on one code system, and the codes it asked for before that
combination simplified.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the role-keyed axis the request left unnamed and the engine defaulted

members.title: Members
members.description: every entity on axis this Spec's read plan serves, sorted by ref; each carries role == axis and a best-effort label/entity_type from a batched graph read, None when the graph has neither

ResolvedScope.title: ResolvedScope
ResolvedScope.description:
The full member set of an entity axis this Spec's request left unnamed
(see ResolvedSpec.scope).

``axis`` is observationAbout when place defaulting expanded a place-less
request, and origin or destination when directional-role defaulting
expanded a role-bearing request. ``members`` lists the entities on that axis
the answer's read plan serves, the ones a coverage breadth dimension for the
same axis counts. members is the single-element ["Earth"] list when the query
resolved as a worldwide total.
The response-level diagnostics may include place_scope_defaulted or
role_scope_defaulted for such resolution, but those warnings are not a
per-Spec one-to-one representation of this field. The scope lives outside
BaseIdentity, the spec hash, and resolved.entities: a resubmit of the
same definition rediscovers it from the live graph.

slots.title: Slots
slots.description: one entry per slot the shape defines, each in a binding state. Its what/how entries are the identity's slots, so a what/how property it leaves out is one no served member asserts

inapplicable_slots.title: Inapplicable Slots
inapplicable_slots.description: the slots whose property none of the resolved StatVars declares, listed by property dcid; empty when every slot applies. Joins to resolved.slots[*].key.property.ref. Applicability is graph state, so it is reported here and the slot itself reads 'unbound' in the definition either way. It is never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

unresolved_slots.title: Unresolved Slots
unresolved_slots.description: the slots whose property is present but unresolved on at least one resolved StatVar (the graph asserted a value for this axis but could not resolve it to a dcid), listed by property dcid; empty when no such slot exists. Joins to resolved.slots[*].key.property.ref, and is disjoint from inapplicable_slots: a property is either never asserted by any resolved StatVar (inapplicable_slots), present but unreadable on one (this field), or neither (a genuinely open axis). The slot itself reads 'unbound' in the definition in every one of these cases; it is never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

stat_vars.description: resolved StatVar(s) inside the region, and the scope they were drawn from

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: resolved entities the data is about; may be empty if where is unbound

entity_groups.title: Entity Groups
entity_groups.description: the named group each role's entities stand for, keyed by the role key the entities above carry: each group whose members are exactly the entities definition.identity binds on that role. The heading names a role by its group and member count ('the 27 EU member states') in place of its members. None when no role was asked for as a group

headline.description: exact latest-year summary for a role-bearing answer (see Headline); None for a non-role-bearing Spec, which coverage above already answers exactly or approximately enough that no separate latest-year summary is computed

download.description: the rows, series, years and licence of the file a mint of this Spec writes (see DownloadFacts). None when the Spec has no read plan: a no-data answer, or same-shape parts merged into one Spec

coverage_stamp.title: Coverage Stamp
coverage_stamp.description: the coverage artifact's own data-version stamp this Spec's role-bearing population and headline were confirmed against (series_coverage.CoverageManifest.stamp); None for a non-role-bearing Spec, which never consults coverage. The graph-derived analogue of this stamp (graph_generation) is not itself a wire field; this is coverage's own, published because coverage is a second, independently-versioned data source an answer can be stale against

scope.description: the full member set of an entity axis this Spec's resolution defaulted (see ResolvedScope): observationAbout for place defaulting, or origin/destination for directional-role defaulting. Response-level diagnostics may carry place_scope_defaulted or role_scope_defaulted, but warning presence is not an exact per-Spec equivalence; None when this Spec did not default an entity axis

facets.title: Facets
facets.description: the facet axis values of the series this Spec's read plan serves, the series its observations carry (see ResolvedFacet); the same whether or not observations are included or deferred to a trailing SSE event. Sparse, meaning an axis no served series carries is omitted, never a null placeholder. {} when the Spec serves no series

observations.description: the observation values behind coverage above; None when not resolved for this Spec (e.g. no entity to probe, or response_options.include_observations is false), when ResolveOptions.include_observations opts into deferred SSE delivery (populated instead via a trailing observations event, mirroring slot_options/entity_options' own coverage-probe transport split), or for a candidates-status entry, nearest_real, or flagged_match spec (this iteration only populates it on a primary definite answer).

slot_options.title: Slot Options
slot_options.description: the candidate set each bound slot was chosen from, one entry per slot with a non-empty taxonomy; omits when/source and any slot with no observed or seeded values. spec_id does not depend on this field, so it never affects permalinks or dedup.

entity_options.title: Entity Options
entity_options.description: candidate sets for directional origin or destination axes. An entry whose entity_ref is omitted describes an axis the role-bearing query left open; its role selects the identity.entities key for a resubmit, and the matching role_axis_facts entry reports that axis's member count. An entry with an entity_ref describes alternatives to a bound axis. Empty when the family has no directional entity-option concept. spec_id does not depend on this field.

facet_options.title: Facet Options
facet_options.description: the candidate set each facet axis (provenance/measurementMethod/unit) was chosen from, one entry per axis with at least one value observed on the resolved candidates' unfiltered facets; an axis with no observed value is omitted, never an empty entry. Computed for every definite Spec and every candidate. Over SSE with response_options.include_option_coverage set, the entries arrive as trailing facet_options events and this list stays empty. Unlike slot_options, this has no bind-time baseline to fall back to. spec_id does not depend on this field.

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: the editable confirmation sentence for this spec, present on every Spec a part shows; None on an equivalent_readings entry. It holds the heading and the byline only (see SentenceToken.segment): 'Germany's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya, 1973 to 2024. Current US dollars · OECD Creditor Reporting System (CRS).' It states what this Spec is and nothing about the request that produced it, so it reads the same after a dataset_resubmit and serves as the Spec's label. The part that carries this Spec states how it departs from the request (_PartBase.departures)

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, tying its tokens to definition parts; present under the same condition, None otherwise. Every token's segment is 'heading' or 'byline'

trace.description: consolidated record of how the query was understood

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: qualitative, relative retrieval confidence for this interpretation; None when not assessed. Bands are heuristic and may be retuned without a schema-version bump.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: why the part offers this Spec as one of its candidates: 'structural', a reading that differs from the elected one only on a stat type, price basis or denominator the request leaves open; 'nominated', a reading the model named as a genuine reading of the request's phrase; 'twin', an equivalent reading of the elected one, offered where the elected one holds no data; 'direction', the same reading with the other direction for a place the request names without one, which a client shows as a direction prompt; 'breakdown', the same measure broken down by another set of slots, offered when its family holds no total and the request names no breakdown that serves a member. The elected reading, listed first, carries none. None on a definite answer and on every Spec outside CandidateSet.specs.

available_at_place.title: Available At Place
available_at_place.description: whether this spec has lifetime availability at the resolved place, independent of the coverage window. True = confirmed at place; False = the variable matched but has no observation here (the flagged_match case); None = not assessed (no place entity, or a named family such as dev-finance). CoverageExact.has_data may be False for a requested window even when this field is True.

equivalent_readings.title: Equivalent Readings
equivalent_readings.description: other StatVar(s) confirmed to encode the same real-world indicator as this Spec. Each entry is a full Spec carrying identity and the material needed to re-resolve onto it: its definition.identity, spec_id, and resolved StatVar dcids provide everything ResubmitIdentityPayload requires. Its rendered_sentence, sentence_plan, facet_options, and observations come from re-resolving onto it on a dataset_resubmit identity entry, not from this response. This Spec's own answer stands on its own regardless. Switching to a named entry is optional, offered for its source vocabulary's own coverage. None when no such encoding is known. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed, and never populated on its own entries in turn. An entry's own equivalent_readings is always empty.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: ids of the skills this Spec's bound graph nodes and selected provenance call for, matched against the shared skills index, most specific first: skills matched through a graph node by hop, then breadth, and skills matched only through the provenance last; present under the include_skills option. None = the request did not ask; [] = it asked and nothing matched.

alternative_measures.title: Alternative Measures
alternative_measures.description: every other measure this Spec could equally answer with -- either another populated partition from the same family as the one this Spec's own served rows exhibit (retrieval.bound_values.observed_measure_family), or a genuinely distinct also_plausible candidate whose only difference from this Spec is measured_property (measurement_denominator held equal), folded in here instead of left as a second candidates entry -- each with its own identity, a disambiguating label, and the axis of the sentence token whose menu offers it: 'what' entries are the measure switch beside measure_label below, 'unit' entries the price-basis options of the byline's unit token (binding_ref 'unit:'). A partition or folded candidate with no authored label is left out. None when this Spec's shape carries no measure family at all and no measure-sibling candidate was folded in, or its served rows span more than one partition; a served partition with every sibling unlabelled, or with none, still publishes []. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

measure_label.title: Measure Label
measure_label.description: the readable label for the measure partition this Spec's own served rows exhibit, composed the same way as each 'what' alternative_measures entry's label: what a switch built from those entries would show as currently selected. It names no price basis ('gross disbursements', not 'gross disbursements (nominal)'). Current or constant prices belong to the unit, which the byline's unit token states. None under the same condition alternative_measures is None

measure_label_axes.title: Measure Label Axes
measure_label_axes.description: the declared measure-axis identifiers (code_index.types.MeasureAxis.axis, e.g. 'measuredProperty', 'measurementQualifier', or a constraint-property dcid such as a financial-flow-type or netting-basis axis) that measure_label was composed from. Every axis the served partition carries a value on is included here, whether or not its value appears in measure_label's own text. A renderer uses this to keep a bound how-slot sharing one of these property dcids from repeating what measure_label already said. Always [] when measure_label is None.

measure_axis_values.title: Measure Axis Values
measure_axis_values.description: each axis in measure_label_axes with the value the served partition holds on it, in the same order, including values the query never named (a declared default such as Gross or Nominal). Labels come from the measure index. Always [] when measure_label is None. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

related_group.description: the StatVarGroup related_measures come from: the smallest group this Spec's one StatVar belongs to that holds 2 to 40 members, ties broken by group dcid. None when related_measures is None or []

related_measures.title: Related Measures
related_measures.description: up to 5 other members of related_group with data at every place this Spec names (and in its requested years when it names a range), ordered by the years they share with this Spec's StatVar there, then by dcid. Only a definite Spec that serves exactly one StatVar, has no measure family (measure_label is None) and names places with no roles carries a list; [] when no group qualifies or no other member has data there. None for any other Spec, and when the graph reads failed or ran past their deadline. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

open_axis_facts.title: Open Axis Facts
open_axis_facts.description: one entry per constraint axis this Spec's own served StatVar members declare (an arc naming the property, resolved or not) that the query left unbound, each naming the axis's property and what those members exhibit on it: whether they agree on a value (varies=False) or differ (varies=True), and undeclared_count for how many declare none at all. None when this Spec's served members declare no constraint property the query left open at all. This is distinct from an open axis every member declares nothing for, which still publishes its own entry (varies=False, undeclared_count equal to the served member count). Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

role_axis_facts.title: Role Axis Facts
role_axis_facts.description: one entry per directional role axis (origin/destination) this role-bearing Spec's query left open, naming the axis and the member population its own confirmation already resolved (see RoleAxisFact). None when this Spec is not role-bearing, or is role-bearing but every role axis its shape declares carries a bound entity. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

unit_conversion.description: the currencies and price bases a unit request can convert this answer to. Null when the served members' unit is no currency, no conversion recipe converts them (a stock, a series not in nominal prices, or a provenance that declares no recipe), the recipe's tables lack the native currency's rate in a served year, so nothing converts, or no conversion catalogue is loaded, which the part's unit_conversion_unavailable warning states. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

ResolvedSpec.title: ResolvedSpec
ResolvedSpec.description:
What the graph held at resolution time: the engine's report of what it
did with the ask. Meant for display and diagnostics, never hashed;
`Spec.spec_id` depends only on `Spec.definition.identity`. Beside the
contract's own `resolved` member list (`stat_vars`, `inapplicable_slots`,
`unresolved_slots`, `entities`, `coverage`, `headline`, `facets`, `observations`,
`rendered_sentence`/`sentence_plan`, `slot_options`/`entity_options`,
`trace`, `confidence`), this also carries the engine's own supersets
(`shape`, `slots`, `available_at_place`) that slot_options/sentence_plan
join against and the eval harness scores.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: how many members are confirmed to carry observations at this resolve's own probe entities; see this model's own docstring for how this differs from resolved.shape.member_count

member_count_exact.title: Member Count Exact
member_count_exact.description: True when member_count is a true total; False when it is a floor -- the population being at least member_count large, not exactly member_count -- because it was measured over a capped recall sample, because the probe stopped once the answer's member was confirmed, or because it is a where-axis merge's max() of its members' own counts rather than a computed union. Defaults to True, correct for a caller that has not measured otherwise

served_count.title: Served Count
served_count.description: how many StatVars a Datasets mint of this Spec's definition serves, the length of its trace.resolved_stat_vars; 1 for a single series. Null when the membership is unsettled: Search answered from members the mint may not serve, and the part carries membership_unverified

data_date_range.description: the earliest first date and latest last date of the points the answer's read plan serves over its StatVars; null when it serves none

source_codes.title: Source Codes
source_codes.description: the publisher series codes of the StatVars the answer serves, sorted by provenance then code and without repeats; left out when no served StatVar has a code. They identify the series a publisher files these StatVars under, and the answer is the same with or without them. A code names the whole answer only where its entry is exact

ResolvedStatVars.title: ResolvedStatVars
ResolvedStatVars.description:
`resolved.stat_vars` on the wire: how many StatVars the answer holds, how many a
Datasets mint of the Spec's definition serves, and the dates the answer serves over
them. The members themselves stay off the wire; `POST /api/datasets/{id}/members`
lists the ones a mint serves.

member_count is the population confirmed to carry observations at this
resolve's own probe entities, not resolved.shape.member_count's
bindings-admitted population. The two differ for two reasons. A member the
shape's bindings admit can carry no observation at the resolved place. And on
a role-bearing shape the answer reads one role class of the admitted members:
where a total stands for its breakdowns the breakdowns are folded into it, so a
donor-only answer can state 255 admitted members beside 1 confirmed while every
one of the 255 holds data. On a standard (non-role-bearing) shape this population can itself
be a floor: the packaged code index does not source members for every
shape family, so a shape outside it falls back to its recall sample, the
members recall found, and member_count cannot exceed what that sample
admitted. An answer naming one member of a family too large for one read stops
reading once that member is confirmed, so member_count counts the members read: "latest
life expectancy data" reads the family's total and not its other 350 members. A
where-axis merge (same_shape.py, "population
of Kenya and Uganda") publishes max() of its members' own member_count
rather than the sum, since the same StatVar is typically confirmed at
every member's own place and summing would double-count the
intersection -- max() is a true lower bound of the union. member_count_exact
records which of these applies.

served_count is the mint's own count, a function of the definition alone: the
StatVars a Datasets mint of `definition` serves, the length of its
`trace.resolved_stat_vars`. It is stated whenever Search settled the membership the
mint resolves: a family the code index decides, or a family the mint's member walk
settled for this definition. Null when Search answers from members it could not
settle, which the part flags with a `membership_unverified` warning.

entity_groups.title: Entity Groups
entity_groups.description: the named group each role's entities were asked for as, keyed by entity role key. Post a prior Spec's resolved.entity_groups beside any identity derived from that Spec. A group is kept when it posts a dcid and the graph's members of that node are exactly the identity's entities on the role; any other group, including one on a role the identity binds no entity on, is dropped

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: the assumptions of the reading this candidate rebuilds, echoed as the response gave them, which are the candidates part's reading_assumptions under the reading's spec_id. The rebuilt reading's reading_assumptions entry states the echoed items that still hold, each worded from the rebuilt reading by the rule ResubmitIdentityEntry.assumptions states, and the rebuilt part's assumptions are the items every reading_assumptions list holds alike. An item the echo lacks is not stated, so an edit of a defaulted slot to another value drops that default, and [], the echo of a reading that stated none, states none. None, the default, means the client echoes nothing for this reading, which yields what a fresh request would: no declared default, since the posted identity binds every slot, and the open roles and place scope the reading reads

ResubmitCandidate.title: ResubmitCandidate
ResubmitCandidate.description:
One candidate identity within a `candidates` dataset_resubmit entry. The
engine derives its StatVar members as it does for an identity entry.

entry_kind.title: Entry Kind
entry_kind.description: discriminator for a candidate-set dataset_resubmit entry

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: this part's variable text, echoed back onto the rebuilt part

ordering.title: Ordering
ordering.description: how `candidates` below was ordered when this set was first produced; echoed back verbatim onto the rebuilt candidates part, never recomputed

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: echoed back verbatim onto the rebuilt candidates part -- see CandidateSet.truncated for what this flags

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: the competing candidates to re-materialise, in posted order, always -- the rebuilt CandidateSet.specs preserves this exact order. Refused request_invalid, at the engine rather than here, when the posted count exceeds this deployment's own ceiling -- readable in advance as caps.max_candidates from GET /api/search/capabilities

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them; it is kept apart from same-shape sibling parts. False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

ResubmitCandidatesEntry.title: ResubmitCandidatesEntry
ResubmitCandidatesEntry.description:
One part re-materialised from a posted set of competing candidate
identities, through the promote path, in posted order, always. `ordering`
names the display rule this set already used, restated rather than
recomputed: the order rests on the bind model's election and the availability
reads of the first answer, which do not round-trip -- see `Ordering` and
`outcomes.CandidateSet`. This entry carries no
`max_candidates` field: `CandidateSet.max_candidates` on the response is
not posted back and is always server-computed, never client-supplied.

entry_kind.title: Entry Kind
entry_kind.description: discriminator for a single-identity dataset_resubmit entry

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: this part's variable text, echoed back onto the rebuilt part

identity.description: the complete identity. Post a prior Spec.definition.identity byte-for-byte for a no-op resubmit; change nested members, including entities.origin or entities.destination, to edit that definition

entity_groups.title: Entity Groups
entity_groups.description: the named group each role's entities were asked for as, keyed by entity role key. Post a prior Spec's resolved.entity_groups beside any identity derived from that Spec. A group is kept when it posts a dcid and the graph's members of that node are exactly the identity's entities on the role; any other group, including one on a role the identity binds no entity on, is dropped

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them; it is kept apart from same-shape sibling parts. False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: the assumptions of the part this entry rebuilds, echoed as the response gave them. For a definite part these are its assumptions. For a reading picked from a candidates part they are that part's reading_assumptions under the reading's spec_id. The rebuilt part states the echoed items that still hold, each worded from the rebuilt answer: a declared_default whose slot (binding_ref) still binds the echoed refs, an open_role whose axis the answer still reads across every member with no entity of the identity's, and a place_scope on an answer that still names no place. An item the echo lacks is not stated, since the posted identity or its edit asked for it. An edit of a defaulted slot to another value therefore drops that default, and [], the echo of a part that stated none, states none. None, the default, means the client echoes nothing, and the part states what a fresh request would: no declared default, since the posted identity binds every slot, and the open roles and place scope the answer reads. The engine cannot tell an echoed default from one the caller writes for a slot it chose itself, and states such an item while the slot binds its refs. An echo shapes only the caller's own response

ResubmitIdentityEntry.title: ResubmitIdentityEntry
ResubmitIdentityEntry.description:
One part re-resolved from a single identity -- the payload
`ResubmitIdentityPayload` carries, plus the text echo and operations every
dataset_resubmit entry needs.

entry_kind.title: Entry Kind
entry_kind.description: discriminator for a re-parsed dataset_resubmit entry

part.description: this part's resolution inputs -- normally a prior response part's own Part.restatement, posted back verbatim or edited, and resolved through the same per-part machinery the parsed door uses

ResubmitParsedEntry.title: ResubmitParsedEntry
ResubmitParsedEntry.description:
One part genuinely re-resolved through the parsed door's own per-part
path, from a client-edited restatement of a sibling's own resolution
inputs (`Part.restatement`) -- re-parsed, where `placeholder` only
restates a stub. `part` already carries a required `variable_text` and
its own `operations`, so this entry needs no separate top-level echo
fields the way the other three kinds do. Costs one LLM bind per edit, the
door's one entry kind that touches the LLM client at all.

entry_kind.title: Entry Kind
entry_kind.description: discriminator for a stub dataset_resubmit entry

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: this part's variable text, echoed back onto the rebuilt part

status.title: Status
status.description: which stub outcome to restate for this part

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: the NoData.reason to restate onto the rebuilt part; required when status is no_data, refused when status is unsupported

code.title: Code
code.description: the reason, a code from the platform registry, to restate onto the rebuilt part's Unsupported.code; required when status is unsupported, refused when status is no_data

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them; it is kept apart from same-shape sibling parts. False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

ResubmitPlaceholderEntry.title: ResubmitPlaceholderEntry
ResubmitPlaceholderEntry.description:
One part restated as a stub from a no_data/unsupported outcome the
client already holds -- zero graph round-trips, zero LLM calls. Carried
forward unresolved so its sibling parts' composed sentence and fold can
still be computed across the whole dataset; the engine stamps a
part-scoped `part_restated` info warning on the rebuilt part.

pinned.title: Pinned
pinned.description: whether the frame the version's files render from is in the pinned tier, which has no expiry

held_until.title: Held Until
held_until.description: when the working-tier frame stops being guaranteed, 30 days after it was stored. A download of the frame after `held_until`, while its bytes survive, renews it for 30 days. After it, a file selector or download link request that must render its file again renews the frame for 30 days if the frame's bytes survive, and otherwise refuses `artifact_expired`. A rebuild of unchanged data through `GET /api/datasets/{id}` or `POST /api/datasets` stores the frame again. Absent when pinned. It can be in the past

RetentionModel.title: RetentionModel
RetentionModel.description:
How long a version can still be fetched, which `datasets_api.retention` computes when a
door serves the version. No stored body holds it.

role.description: which flow axis this fact is about

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: how many entities this axis' open scope resolves to, leaving out the group totals the code index declares beside their members (party_kind total), as the default download leaves them out; a scope of totals alone counts them all. None when the count could not be established without a read this response chose not to make (e.g. a discovered opposite axis whose own role index was omitted after a cap trip); the fact still publishes in that case, naming the axis as open with an explicit unknown rather than staying silent about it

members_available.title: Members Available
members_available.description: whether the member list this count summarises is itself known and could be enumerated (e.g. through entity_options or the options door), not just counted. False exactly when member_count is None

RoleAxisFact.title: RoleAxisFact
RoleAxisFact.description:
One directional role axis (origin or destination) a role-bearing
Spec's query left open, and what this Spec's own confirmation already
knows about its member scope (see ResolvedSpec.role_axis_facts).

Unlike OpenConstraintAxisFact, a role axis has no declared value of its
own that could vary across served members -- the axis is a place a flow
entity binds, not a constraint members assert -- so this carries no
varies/undeclared_count of its own; it carries only what a role axis
genuinely has: a population size and whether that population is known.

count.title: Count
count.description: codes for a code system, members under the default projection for a group or region, Datasets for a source

RootEntry.title: GraphRootEntry
RootEntry.description: A place to start listing from, with the length of its list.

built_from.title: Built From
built_from.description: the build of each table the document read

Roots.title: GraphRoots
Roots.description: `GET /api/graph/roots`: where to start listing. Each list is ordered by dcid.

window.title: Window
window.description: the years to serve. Replaces the spec's window whole

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: role name to dcids. Replaces the spec's whole entity binding. A role this map omits is unbound, so a client narrowing one role repeats the spec's other roles, and {} unbinds every bound role. An open role the map binds is no longer open

facets.title: Facets
facets.description: axis to binding. Replaces the spec's whole facet binding

Scope-Input.title: Scope
Scope-Input.description:
The `scope` block a mint request may carry. On a `spec_id` input each
supplied member replaces the stored spec's value for that member whole,
and an omitted member keeps the spec's value. On a `statvar_set` input,
which has no stored spec, an omitted member is unbound (everything).
`window` narrows the result to `all`, `latest`, or a
`start_year`/`end_year` range. `entities` binds role names to non-empty
lists of dcids (a role's values must each be non-empty and must not
contain `+` or `,`). `facets` binds a known axis (`provenance`,
`measurementMethod`, `unit`) to a specific ref, or `measurementMethod`
or `unit` to a null ref. The `unit` axis alone may instead carry a
conversion request (`FacetUnitRequestBinding`) or ask for each entity's
own currency (`FacetNationalCurrencyBinding`).

place.description: the country the question named, when the engine confirmed it as a country; null when the question named no place or named one that is not a confirmed country

Scope-Output.title: AnswerScope
Scope-Output.description:
What a catalogue or declined answer was scoped to. Titled apart from the
datasets API's own `Scope`, which the composed app's OpenAPI also publishes.

ScopeAndUnits.title: ScopeAndUnits
ScopeAndUnits.description:
`countries` is always `[]`. `years_covered` is filled where the graph
has it. `currencies` lists every currency unit the coverage index gives the
source's Provenances, sorted, and `granularity` is filled where it gives
one period and axis pair for the source.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: 'text' is invariant wording: a connective carrying its own surrounding whitespace (' for ', ' to '), a possessive suffix ("'s"), a bare ' '/', ' separator, the terminal '.', or a departure sentence; 'slot' is a slot- or entity-bound phrase, or on an entity_ambiguous no_data plan the ambiguous wording itself, which a client hangs the candidate menu on. A client that does not recognise a kind should render its text as plain text regardless.

text.title: Text
text.description: the rendered text for this token; empty string for a slot with nothing bound

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the grammatical axis this token fills, when kind=='slot': one of the request-slot axes, 'unit' for the byline's unit of measure, or 'method' for the byline's measurement method, which no request slot carries. The unit token's binding_ref is 'unit:', and its options are the Spec's resolved.alternative_measures entries with axis 'unit': the price-basis siblings (current and constant prices) where the graph holds both. The method token appears only when the identity binds measurementMethod (a ref, a null ref, or a set), after the source token; its binding_ref is 'method:', its text the bound method's label without a trailing full stop or 'No stated method' for a null ref, and its options the Spec's facet_options entry with axis 'measurementMethod'

segment.title: Segment
segment.description: the part of the sentence this token belongs to: 'coverage' (the 'Answered N of M parts.' a mixed envelope sentence opens with, never on a part's or a Spec's own plan), 'heading' (what the answer is), 'byline' (latest-year label, unit, source, and a bound method), 'departure' (the text of one Departure on the same part, never on a Spec's own plan), or 'assumption' (the closing clause naming what the answer assumed, from the parts' assumptions, never on a Spec's own plan). A client styles each segment as a block; the plain join of every token's text still equals rendered_sentence

property_dcid.title: Property Dcid
property_dcid.description: the constraint property dcid this token renders, when one exists; null or omitted for property-less axes (when/source), for a shape-label fallback phrase with no backing slot, and for entity-role tokens with no backing where slot. Set on a 'destination' entity-role token when the shape declares a where slot backing that axis (e.g. dev-finance).

role.description: origin/destination when this token renders a directional entity role (the flow's two endpoints read back), or the directional scope an unbound where slot resolved to. entity_refs is the discriminator: non-empty on the entity read-back, empty on the unbound-where-slot fallback. binding_ref is not: an entity read-back carries binding_ref too whenever the shape declares a where slot backing the 'destination' axis (e.g. dev-finance), the same condition under which the unbound-where-slot fallback always carries it, so a present binding_ref value never separates the two. Both kinds join to the Spec.resolved.entity_options entry on the same role. A third token sits on an entity_ambiguous no_data plan, which has no Spec: the ambiguous wording, with the role the request gave it (null when it gave none), no entity_refs and no binding_ref, and text equal to one NoData.ambiguous_entities[i].text on the same part, the i its entity_choice names. The client titles that wording's candidate menu by this role and posts the pick's entry of NoData.options.

entity_choice.title: Entity Choice
entity_choice.description: on the slot token an entity_ambiguous no_data plan marks for an ambiguous wording, the index into NoData.ambiguous_entities of the group it asks, on the part its part_index names in an envelope plan. The NoData.options with the same entity_choice form that slot's menu. Null on every other token

binding_ref.title: Binding Ref
binding_ref.description: join key correlating this token to its Spec.resolved.slots / SlotOptions entry: 'axis:property_dcid', i.e. SlotKey.as_ref() (matching Slot.key and SlotOptions.key). Set for a slot-backed token, and also for a 'destination' entity-role token when the shape declares a where slot backing that axis (e.g. dev-finance) -- see entity_refs for the entity side of that token. The byline's unit token carries 'unit:', which no slot backs; its options are the resolved.alternative_measures entries with axis 'unit'. The byline's method token carries 'method:', which no slot backs either. Null or omitted for plain connective text, a shape-label fallback phrase with no backing slot, and 'origin'/unbacked-'destination' entity-role tokens.

entity_refs.title: Entity Refs
entity_refs.description: entity dcids this token renders, set on the entity read-back, one of the two token kinds role marks (see role's own docstring for the other, the unbound-where-slot fallback, which leaves entity_refs empty even though it too carries role) -- a directional entity read-back has no Spec.resolved.slots entry of its own, though a 'destination' token may additionally carry binding_ref when a backing where slot exists (e.g. dev-finance); one dcid per entity in the token's group, in the same order as the entities joined into this token's text -- e.g. a 'destination' token reading 'Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda' carries all three dcids, so a client can tell a 3-entity answer from a 1-entity one without parsing rendered text. Empty when role is unset, and this emptiness, not binding_ref, is the join rule that separates the two role-bearing kinds.

states.title: States
states.description: the refs a heading or byline slot token states, so a client edits each from this token: its own binding_ref, then each binding the renderer left silent because this token's text already says it. Refs read as binding_ref does ('how:crsTypeOfFlow', 'where:', 'origin:', 'unit:'), plus 'axis:<property dcid>' for a measure axis no slot carries ('axis:nettingBasis'). The measure noun states the measure axes its label or authored noun carries, the how values it names, and the agreed open axes beside it; a StatVar name or graph name states the how values it folds. The byline's unit token states 'unit:' and, when it names a price basis, the measurementQualifier axis. The byline's source token states 'source:', which is also its binding_ref where the answer binds a source slot. The byline's method token states 'method:', its binding_ref, and while the identity binds no method no token states 'method:'. Empty on a token with empty text, on text tokens, and outside heading and byline slot tokens. Within one part, no ref appears on two tokens with text. A bound slot, an unbound slot with options, or a role that no token states is stated nowhere in the sentence (a boolean member, an adjectival fold dropped whole, an open role with no count), and a client offers it apart from the sentence with its current value. On the envelope plan a token with no part_index states its refs for every part it stands for

distinguishes.title: Distinguishes
distinguishes.description: true when this token's text differs from the same-bucket text on another candidate in the same CandidateSet; null or omitted on every other token, including every token on a Spec rendered outside a candidate set

part_index.title: Part Index
part_index.description: this token's position in Resolution.parts, when this plan is the envelope-level composed sentence (Resolution.sentence_plan) and this token belongs to exactly one part's own contribution -- a variable phrase token, or a qualifier attached to it because it did not agree across every part, or a token of a part composed as its own sentence. Null carries four distinct readings a client must not conflate: on a part's own plan (DefinitePart.spec.resolved.sentence_plan, or the candidates/no_data/unsupported sentence_plan on _PartBase) the field has no meaning at all and is never set; on a composer-minted token, it means the token belongs to the sentence as a whole rather than to any one part (the Oxford-joined ' and '/', ', the plan's own terminal '.', the shared ' ' the per-part fallback puts between two sentences, the 'coverage' opener, and an assumptions clause's lead, separators and '.' when no one part carries every item it names are all such tokens); on a token every contributing part states alike and the join states once (a hoisted qualifier on the where, when, or source axis, each a wire value of axis, or the origin role, identified by role=='origin' instead since SentenceAxis has no 'origin' member; a shared possessive lead; the shared byline; or a heading or byline token of a part a later part folded into, binding_folded, which both parts state) it means the token no longer describes a single variable; and on an 'assumption' item it means more than one part assumed it, and each part's own assumptions list says which.

SentenceToken.title: SentenceToken
SentenceToken.description:
One token in the ordered sentence plan: a "text" token (invariant
wording such as a connective, a bare separator, the terminal period, or a
departure sentence) or a "slot" token (a slot- or entity-bound phrase, or
the wording of an ambiguous entity).

``rendered_sentence`` (the flat string) is the plain concatenation of every
token's ``text``, in order. The two are computed together and cannot drift.
A "slot" token with nothing bound appears too, with ``text=""``: the same
token structure serves a loading skeleton (before binding is known) and the
final sentence (after it is). The first non-empty token's text is
capitalised.

Every token belongs to one ``segment``. The heading states what the answer
is: actor, measure noun, counterpart, and period, in possessive order, one
slot token per axis ("Germany's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya, 1973 to
2024"). A unit that changes the magnitude (per capita, percent of GDP, PPP
international dollars) stays in the heading. The byline follows it: the
latest-year label when one applies, the plain unit with its price basis
("current US dollars", "constant 2022 US dollars") as a slot token with
axis "unit", the source, and, when the identity binds measurementMethod, the
method as a slot token with axis "method". Departures come next, then the
assumptions clause, and both sit only on a part's or the envelope's sentence, so
``spec.resolved.sentence_plan`` carries neither.

measurement_method.description: null when no facet states a method: no stated method

Series.title: GraphAvailabilitySeries
Series.description: A source's facets sharing a measurement method, period and scaling.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the dcid of the value the StatVar holds on property

label.title: Label
label.description: display label for ref: its graph label, else the dcid's tail split into lower-case words

SeriesAxisRef.title: SeriesAxisRef
SeriesAxisRef.description: One constraint of a series' StatVar (see ObservationSeries.axes).

entity.title: Entity
entity.description: the entity dcid absent from the deflator table

fallback_entity.title: Fallback Entity
fallback_entity.description: the recipe's fallback entity substituted for it

SeriesConversionFallbackExample.title: SeriesConversionFallbackExample
SeriesConversionFallbackExample.description:
One entity a converted series' recipe substituted with its own
fallback entity, because the substituted entity carried no row at all
in the deflator table (see ObservationSeriesConversion.fallback_examples).

label.title: Label
label.description: best-effort display label for ref; None when unresolved, never fabricated

party_kind.title: Party Kind
party_kind.description: on an origin or destination entity, what the party is beside the others on its side: 'party' (a country, territory or organisation), 'total' (other parties' figures, so a sum across the role that counts it counts its members twice) or 'residual' (figures no other party holds), as the code index lists it. Absent for a party the index does not list, and on observationAbout

SeriesEntityRef.title: SeriesEntityRef
SeriesEntityRef.description: One entity in a series' role tuple (see ObservationSeries.entities).

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the facet's dcid for this axis

label.title: Label
label.description: best-effort display label for ref; None when unresolved, never fabricated

source.description: provenance axis only: the organisation behind the provenance, from the origin catalogue; absent for a provenance the catalogue does not list

data_commons.description: provenance axis only: the Data Commons the provenance's data comes from; absent for a provenance the catalogue does not list

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.description: provenance axis only: the Graph API route of the provenance's document, GET /api/graph/documentation/{dcid}

SeriesFacetRef.title: SeriesFacetRef
SeriesFacetRef.description:
One axis's value on a single series' selected observation facet (see
ObservationSeries.facet).

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the StatVar dcid these points observe

label.title: Label
label.description: a row's own distinguishing label: composed from ref's own constraint values when it has any beyond its shape's shared five-tuple, else ref's plain resolved display name; None when unresolved, never fabricated

SeriesStatVarRef.title: SeriesStatVarRef
SeriesStatVarRef.description: A series' StatVar identity ({ref, label} -- mirrors SeriesFacetRef's shape).

ServedMember.title: ServedMember
ServedMember.description:
One StatVar a definition serves: its `dcid:`-prefixed `ref`, as the manifest trace's
`resolved_stat_vars` names it, its graph `label` (`null` when the graph holds none), the
`roles` it declares, and its `constraints`, each constraint property with its value
(`null` when the StatVar leaves it unbound).

shape_id.title: Shape Id
shape_id.description: stable id of this structural family

label.title: Label
label.description: plain-language name of what the reading serves: a composed measure label, the served series' name, or the family's name

population_type.description: the graph populationType; None when the StatVar does not assert it (custom-DC imports may omit any five-tuple arc)

measured_property.description: the graph measuredProperty; None when the StatVar does not assert it (custom-DC imports may omit any five-tuple arc)

stat_type.description: the graph statType, e.g. measuredValue; None when the StatVar does not assert it (custom-DC imports may omit any five-tuple arc)

measurement_qualifier.description: structural anchor; present only when the measured property is qualified

measurement_denominator.description: a structural anchor, present only on a ratio or per-capita measure. Holds the measurementDenominator arc's target dcid for a resolved StatVar or for a dangling target that itself carries a dcid. Is None both when no denominator arc exists at all and when the arc's target carries no dcid. A null value here does not by itself establish that no denominator arc exists. Read measurement_denominator_unresolved alongside it to tell the two apart

measurement_denominator_unresolved.title: Measurement Denominator Unresolved
measurement_denominator_unresolved.description: true when the measurementDenominator arc is present and its target is a ProvisionalNode the graph defines no real StatVar for, whether or not that target carries a dcid. False when no denominator arc exists at all, or when the arc names a confirmed StatVar. A client should read this flag before trusting measurement_denominator on its own. A null ref is consistent with either no arc (this flag false) or a dcid-less dangling target (this flag true), and a populated ref is consistent with either a confirmed StatVar (this flag false) or a dcid-bearing dangling target (this flag true)

slot_keys.title: Slot Keys
slot_keys.description: the constraint and facet slots this family exposes, in display order

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: the size of the resolved population behind this response: how many StatVars the shape's current bindings admit, narrowing as a slot binds and widening again as one is cleared

member_digest.title: Member Digest
member_digest.description: lowercase sha256 hex of the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the sorted list of bare dcids (no 'dcid:' prefix) of the family a Datasets mint of this Spec's definition resolves, the mint's trace.family_member_digest: every row of the family the code index resolves, or every member the mint's member walk confirms when it read every candidate. Null when Search did not settle that family for this definition, and when its walk proved the members from a window it did not read to the end, so it cannot name every member of the family

refine_supported.title: Refine Supported
refine_supported.description: true unless the shape's StatVar(s) are ratio-backed (with _AsAFractionOf_ tokens), which construct-and-confirm sibling StatVars cannot refine

data_commons.title: Data Commons
data_commons.description: every Data Commons holding admitted data for a member StatVar, in the order dfo, base, un_system; a Data Commons by Google variable lists dfo as well when the Observatory's own imports hold it. Empty when the engine derived the shape without its members

upstream.description: the one source and Data Commons every member's data comes through, present only for a shape outside the Observatory's own imports whose members the origin catalogue places under exactly one source

Shape.title: Shape
Shape.description: The structural family chosen for the query.

source.description: the organisation behind every member's data

data_commons.description: the Data Commons serving that data

ShapeUpstream.title: ShapeUpstream
ShapeUpstream.description:
The one source, and the Data Commons serving it, behind every member of
an upstream shape.

SimpleUnit.title: SimpleUnit
SimpleUnit.description:
A unit by reference, by currency, or both, with optional words.

`ref` is the unit's dcid. `currency` is an ISO 4217 code, which a converted unit
`{currency, prices, base_year}` names in place of a dcid. `prices` says whether money is
in `current` or `constant` prices, and `base_year` names the year constant prices are
expressed in; it is present exactly when prices are constant.

id.title: Id
id.description: the skill's stable id; the key this entry is filed under

description.title: Description
description.description: the skill's declared description

content_version.title: Content Version
content_version.description: sha256: over the skill's manifest, SKILL.md then its references in path order, so any edit to any file in the bundle changes it

Skill.title: Skill
Skill.description:
One skill's front matter on the wire, keyed by id in
Resolution.skills. Mirrors skills_index.SkillFrontMatter's four
members -- the search API's own wire model, not that dataclass itself,
so it carries its own field descriptions the way every other response
model does.

key.description: the slot's typed identity (axis + property + label)

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: exactly one of the three binding states

expansion.description: codes the resolver admitted beyond this slot's own bound value(s), when the bound value's code system is declared hierarchical; None for every other slot, including one bound on a flat code system (e.g. crsTypeOfFlow) or a property the deployment's code index does not carry at all. Reports resolution-time breadth only -- `binding` alone is what the query asked for and what spec identity hashes.

summable.title: Summable
summable.description: true when the datasets door's `groupby` sums the family's members over this slot into one complete series: the slot's property is a code system the deployment's code index declares summable (capabilities `summable_axes`), and the dataset the family is served from declares that an observation it carries no row for reads as zero, so a member with no rows adds nothing. False for every other property, for the property that classifies a dataset's rows, and for every slot of a family whose dataset declares no such reading, where a member with no rows refuses the sum. Independent of the binding, so an unbound, set or value-bound slot reads alike. Spec identity does not hash it.

Slot.title: Slot
Slot.description: One slot in the chosen shape, with its current binding state.

property.description: the constraint property that defines this slot when one exists; null or omitted for when, source, and the where-axis slot that binds the subject/destination entity directly (no constraint property backs it)

label.title: Label
label.description: human label, e.g. purpose, donor

SlotKey.title: SlotKey
SlotKey.description: A slot's typed identity: axis, constraint property, and human label.

value.description: one taxonomy member or observed facet value

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: this option's observation footprint if it were bound instead of the current value; populated when response_options.include_option_coverage is true

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: where this option sits in a level-scoped constraint-slot menu on a code-index-carried taxonomy: 'child' or 'parent' of the slot's bound value, and 'root' for every other classification root beside a bound root; for an unbound hierarchical slot, 'root' for a classification root and 'child' for a child of the root named in parent; 'root' for every value of a flat code system. None on every other surface this type serves -- entity_options, facet_options, and the options door's OptionsSet -- none of which classify their candidates by level

parent.title: Parent
parent.description: dcid of this option's parent in a hierarchical code system, for a level-scoped constraint-slot option that has one; None for a root, for a flat code system's values, and on every surface where relation is None

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: how many StatVars this index holds coded directly to this option's value (not a subtree rollup), for a level-scoped constraint-slot option; None on every other surface this type serves -- entity_options, facet_options, and the options door's OptionsSet -- none of which count members from the code index

served_rows.title: Served Rows
served_rows.description: the rows this answer's file would hold if this option were bound instead of the current value, in the terms of ResolvedSpec.download.rows: one per series and year with a point inside the requested window, or under 'latest' one per series holding its StatVar's latest year. A series is a served StatVar carrying the option or one of its code-index descendants (the widening the binder applies to a bound value) at one entity, or donor and recipient pair. An unbound slot counts the answer's own family; a bound slot counts the family with that slot left unbound and every other binding kept. An option this answer would serve nothing for is omitted from the menu, except the slot's current value. None where the option is not counted: on entity_options, facet_options and the options door, and on a bound slot whose family needs graph reads to count, where a trailing slot_options event can supply it. A StatVar the coverage artifact does not hold adds no rows: the count covers the pick's other StatVars, and an option all of whose StatVars are missing from the artifact is omitted

served_rows_exact.title: Served Rows Exact
served_rows_exact.description: true when served_rows equals the download.rows a pick of this option would state; false when it is an upper bound: a counted StatVar whose series sit in more than one facet group (provenance, method and unit) in the window, of which the pick's read elects one; an answer read in bulk whose pick's StatVars sit in more than one facet, since a bulk read elects one; under 'latest', a StatVar with a facet observed more often than yearly; an answer that pins a facet value; a unit request whose conversion cannot be read as download.rows_exact describes, that converts a counted series from a currency the answer does not serve, or whose options the coverage probe counts (a bound slot of a subject-place family, a candidates reading); or a series whose facets carry no complete date list. Null exactly when served_rows is null

party_kind.title: Party Kind
party_kind.description: on an origin or destination entity option, what the party is beside the others on its side: 'party' (a country, territory or organisation), 'total' (other parties' figures, so a sum across the role that counts it counts its members twice) or 'residual' (figures no other party holds), as the code index lists it. Absent for a party the index does not list, and on every other option

SlotOption.title: SlotOption
SlotOption.description: One candidate value the binder had available for a slot.

key.description: the slot identity this option set belongs to

options.title: Options
options.description: candidate values, in taxonomy order; a dcid that failed to resolve a label is omitted rather than fabricated. For a level-scoped constraint slot (relation is populated), this is the bound value's children and parent (for a bound root, its children and every other root), or, when the slot is unbound, each classification root followed by its children -- never deeper levels. A counted menu omits every option its answer would serve nothing for except the slot's current value (see SlotOption.served_rows)

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: false when options is the full known set for this slot at its current level (a curated seed taxonomy, a level-scoped taxonomy sourced from the packaged code index, or an observed taxonomy from the same source, rather than the recalled candidates); true when options is only the values observed among the resolved candidates (bounded by the recall cut, not exhaustive)

source.title: Source
source.description: 'seed' for a hand-curated family taxonomy (e.g. dev-finance scheme/purpose); 'observed' for the union of values seen on the confirmed StatVars or resolved query entities

SlotOptions.title: SlotOptions
SlotOptions.description:
The full candidate set one slot was bound against.

The taxonomy the binder chose from and the options a client can offer the user
are the same artifact; this is that artifact, surfaced per slot. ``key`` matches
the ``SlotKey`` of the corresponding entry in ``Spec.resolved.slots`` (join on axis and
``property.ref``).

ref.description: the graph object bound, when the value is a graph object

value_kind.title: Value Kind
value_kind.description: what kind of value this is

SlotValue.title: SlotValue
SlotValue.description: One taxonomy member or facet value bound to a slot.

places.title: Places
places.description: the places covered by kind; null for a role-bearing variable, and while the places' kinds are unread (a transient gap)

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: the entities covered per graph role; null for any other variable

SourceAvailability.title: GraphAvailabilitySourceEntry
SourceAvailability.description: One source's facets of the variable, and their series.

publisher.description: the source arc's target; null when the node carries no source arc

parent.description: the isPartOf arc's target; null when the node has no parent Dataset

transformation_logic_url.title: Transformation Logic Url
transformation_logic_url.description: the dataTransformationLogic arc's value: a URL to the transformation code

data_commons.description: the Data Commons serving this provenance, from the origin catalogue; null for a provenance the catalogue does not admit, a Dataset, or a Source

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.description: the path of the node's source document

SourceBlock.title: GraphSourceBlock
SourceBlock.description:
A Source, Dataset or Provenance's detail block. `documentation` is the path of the
node's source document on this API.

SourceCatalogue.title: SourceCatalogue
SourceCatalogue.description:
The full `GET /api/graph/sources` response: DFO's sources, then the
origin registry's base Data Commons entries and UN System Data Commons
agencies in registry order, each with the provenances the request's
origin catalogue admits under it, grouped by Dataset. UN agencies are left
out when the UN origin is off. The response has no count and no pagination.

SourceCatalogueEntry.title: SourceCatalogueEntry
SourceCatalogueEntry.description:
One source on one Data Commons, with the datasets this deployment
admits under it and the provenances it excludes. DFO provenances and UN
agencies exclude nothing here.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: the provenance dcid of the publisher that issues the code

code.title: Code
code.description: the publisher's series code, as the publisher writes it

exact.title: Exact
exact.description: true when the answer is the series the provenance files under this code and no other: a part naming the code as its source_code and the provenance as its source accepts this Spec as its answer. The answer reads its observations from the provenance alone, the provenance gives none of the code's StatVars another code, and every StatVar a Datasets mint of the Spec serves is one of the code's. False, the default, is omitted: the code names a StatVar the answer serves, and the answer may hold other series or data of another source

SourceCode.title: SourceCode
SourceCode.description: A publisher's own series code for a StatVar, such as World Bank `DT.TDS.DEGG.CD`.

source.description: the origin registry's source for the documented Provenances, null unless the origin catalogue admits every one of them and they share one

data_commons.description: the Data Commons serving the documented Provenances, null unless the origin catalogue admits every one of them and they share one

source_data_url.title: Source Data Url
source_data_url.description: the file the pipeline downloads, the source's `sourceDataUrl`

data_notes.title: Data Notes
data_notes.description: one caveat per entry, as CommonMark

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: every member path that is null or empty for this source, in spec order, e.g. 'details.citation', 'scope_and_units.countries'

document_errors.title: Document Errors
document_errors.description: each Markdown document the source carries but this door could not serve

url.title: Url
url.description: the licence text on the publisher's site, the source's `license`

text.title: Text
text.description: the user's words naming the source, e.g. 'IDS', 'the OECD' or 'World Bank', without the words that ask for its data ('World Bank' in 'World Bank debt data'). They are matched whole against the names of every admitted publisher, dataset and provenance, and their registered abbreviations, ignoring case, punctuation and a leading 'the'. Included words that match none resolve no_data with source_not_resolved. Excluded words that match none remove nothing and warn query_qualifier_dropped. Words that match two unrelated sources resolve no_data with source_ambiguous, listing both

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: the reference this mention names, when the caller holds one (a provenance dcid, a catalogue Dataset ref or a Source ref), such as a restatement's resolved mention or a NoData.ambiguous_sources candidate carries. It skips matching `text`. A ref the origin catalogue does not admit refuses request_invalid with a pointer to it

polarity.title: Polarity
polarity.description: include to answer from this source, exclude to answer from any other. A part with an included source answers from the included sources only. A part with exclusions alone answers from every admitted source but those

SourceMention.title: SourceMention
SourceMention.description: One data source a part names or excludes, as its words, a reference, or both.

label.title: Label
label.description: the node's name; for a Provenance, its parent Dataset's name where it has one. Null, and named in gaps, when the graph gives none

types.title: Types
types.description: the node's typeOf values, as the graph holds them

description.title: Description
description.description: the node's prose in the graph; null when it has none

links.title: Links
links.description: each list relation the node has, mapped to its route; empty when none

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: the member path of every value this door cannot know

built_from.title: Built From
