spec_id.title: Spec Id
spec_id.description: deterministic hash of (shape + canonical slot bindings); permalink-safe, dedup key, golden-comparison handle, cache key

definition.description: the canonical definition this Spec was resolved from: {schema_version, identity}, the same shape Unsupported.definition uses. definition.identity is the identity-core projection this spec_id was minted from, serialised once and never re-derived; hashing it reproduces spec_id by construction. Post definition.identity back byte-for-byte as ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity to edit this Spec. Directional entities remain nested in identity.entities.

resolved.description: the engine's report of what it did with the ask: stat_vars, entities, coverage, trace, and every other display/diagnostic field. Never hashed; see ResolvedSpec

Spec.title: Spec
Spec.description:
The unit of meaning: one named region of the graph.

Reused as the definite answer, each candidate, and NoData's own
flagged_match/alternate_match (a plain Spec on both). See NoData's own
docstring for the failed-gate code each carries, NoData.gate, kept
structurally outside every identity path. NearestRealSpec (below)
subclasses Spec for NoData.nearest_real, adding the relaxation each
suggestion carries. That stays structurally outside every identity path
the same way (spec_id is computed from bindings, never from the model),
so it cannot perturb spec_id.

definition.description: the alternative measure's own {schema_version, spec_id, identity}

label.title: Label
label.description: readable text for this option, distinct from every other entry's on the same axis. A 'what' entry names the measure without its price basis ('net disbursements'), and differs from measure_label; a 'unit' entry names the prices it switches to ('constant prices')

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the sentence token whose menu offers this entry: 'what', the measure noun, or 'unit', the byline's unit token (SentenceToken.axis 'unit', binding_ref 'unit:'), for a partition that differs from this Spec's only in price basis

measure_axis_values.title: Measure Axis Values
measure_axis_values.description: every axis this measure's partition holds a value on, with that value, in measure-axis declaration order; the same projection as ResolvedSpec.measure_axis_values

served_rows.title: Served Rows
served_rows.description: the rows a resubmit of `definition` would write at this Spec's bound roles, in the terms of download.rows: one per series and year with a point inside the requested window, or under 'latest' one per series holding its StatVar's latest year, a series being a served StatVar at one entity, or donor and recipient pair. A Spec that merges several answers counts at every entity its answers bind. A StatVar the coverage artifact does not hold adds no rows, and a measure that would serve none, including one whose StatVars are all missing from the artifact, is not listed. None where the count needs graph reads (a subject-place family, or a family the code index does not decide), or where the merged answers read different years or coverage

served_rows_exact.title: Served Rows Exact
served_rows_exact.description: true when served_rows equals the download.rows of a resubmit of `definition`; false when it is an upper bound: a counted StatVar whose series sit in more than one facet group (provenance, method and unit) in the window; an answer read in bulk whose measure's StatVars sit in more than one facet; under 'latest', a StatVar with a facet observed more often than yearly; an answer that pins a facet value; or a unit request whose conversion cannot be read as download.rows_exact describes, or that converts a counted series from a currency the answer does not serve. Null exactly when served_rows is null

SpecAlternativeMeasure.title: SpecAlternativeMeasure
SpecAlternativeMeasure.description:
One other measure this Spec could equally answer with (see
ResolvedSpec.alternative_measures): either another populated partition
from the same family as the one this Spec's own served rows exhibit, or
a genuinely distinct also_plausible candidate whose only difference from
this Spec is measured_property (measurement_denominator held equal),
folded in here instead of left as a second candidates entry. Carries its
own identity and a label that disambiguates it.

`definition` is minted by editing this Spec's own already-minted
identity onto this partition's measure axes (retrieval.bound_values.
mint_sibling_identity), an index-scan projection, not a resolution.
Carries identity and a label only: no stat_vars, no coverage, no trace.
ResolvedSpec's own required fields have no defaults, so producing one as
a Spec would mean fabricating a resolution that never ran.

Post `definition` back as `identity` on a dataset_resubmit identity entry to
switch onto this measure: the identity's own what/how slots (this
partition's per-partition-declared axes included, e.g. CRS cooperation
modality) name the family the packaged code index's own election
recovers members from, the same recovery a resubmit of this Spec's own
identity uses.

`axis` names the sentence token whose menu offers the entry. A partition
that differs from this Spec's only in price basis (`measurementQualifier`
`Nominal` or `RealValue`) is a unit option, axis "unit", offered by the
byline's unit token (binding_ref "unit:"). Every other entry is a measure
option, axis "what". The measure menu holds one entry per measure
whatever its price basis, so no two "what" entries differ only in price
basis.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: contract schema version this definition was published under; exactly 1

spec_id.title: Spec Id
spec_id.description: the spec_id minted from `identity`; equals the sibling Spec.spec_id, and is what a detached definition (registry row, permalink) is keyed by

identity.description: the identity-core projection this Spec's spec_id was minted from, serialised once and never re-derived; post it back byte-for-byte as ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity to edit this Spec. Directional edits change identity.entities.origin or identity.entities.destination directly

SpecDefinition.title: SpecDefinition
SpecDefinition.description:
The canonical definition a Spec was resolved from: `{schema_version,
spec_id, identity}`. This is the form the registry stores and permalinks
carry, so it is self-contained. A definition lifted out of its Spec still
names which spec it is.

`identity` is the identity-core projection (see `BaseIdentity`) this
Spec's spec_id was minted from, so hashing `identity` again reproduces
`spec_id` by construction.

`spec_id` is carried here as well as on `Spec.spec_id` deliberately: the
duplication is what makes the definition independently meaningful once
detached from the response that delivered it. The one exception is an
`unsupported` response's definition, which omits it: the request was
valid and understood but never became a resolvable construction, so no
spec_id was ever legitimately minted for it.

SpecIdInput.title: SpecIdInput
SpecIdInput.description:
`kind: "spec_id"` -- an id already in the registry, with an optional
canonical `definition` sidecar. `definition.spec_id`, when supplied,
must equal the outer `spec_id`; the sidecar is required only when the
registry does not already hold `spec_id`.

series.title: Series
series.description: one entry per (stat_var, role tuple) pair with observations

total_obs.title: Total Obs
total_obs.description: total observation count across every series' SELECTED facet, window-filtered to the spec's requested window when one exists -- known even when truncated is true and points are truncated. For a windowed per-pair answer, this is the chosen facet's in-window point count, NOT a raw facet obs_count sum and NOT a union across every facet of the pair -- see ObservationSeries. For a scope-defaulted bulk latest-only answer (no requested window), this sums the coverage probe's all-time obs_count per delivered entity instead: with no window to narrow it, that raw obs_count IS the in-window count

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: false when every series above carries its FULL point set (the whole answer's point count was within the server's inline threshold and each series within its row limit); true when a series was truncated to its latest points only, its total_obs still counting every point

omitted.description: why this payload carries no series, when it doesn't; absent when series is genuinely populated. See ObservationsOmission's own docstring

order.title: Order
order.description: how a role-bearing bulk preview chose the series it shows when it shows fewer than the answer holds: 'ranked' when it read every series and shows the most recent and largest (latest year, then latest value, then identity), 'fixed' when it shows a selection made before any value was read, StatVars newest year first and taken round-robin; absent when every series is shown or the preview is not a role-bearing bulk one

SpecObservations.title: SpecObservations
SpecObservations.description:
The observation values behind a Spec's coverage.

An opt-in bounded preview, or the full series when the resolved answer is
small enough to ship in full -- see truncated. Describes the SAME (stat_var,
entity) selection Spec.resolved.coverage already reports, so the numbers here never
describe a different variable than what coverage summarises.

Each series carries one lead observation facet's points, never a union
across facets: a StatVar/entity pair can have several reporting facets
(e.g. commitments vs disbursements, current vs constant prices), and
merging their points chronologically would interleave same-dated points
from incompatible series into one meaningless line. The one exception is
the same source's estimates continuing the lead past its last period: the
series carries their points after the lead's, `facet` names the lead, and
the `modelled_values` departure marks the estimates. One facet group is
selected per StatVar instead, across every place and role tuple the answer
names: among facets holding a point in the requested years (all facets when
none does), DFO's facets first for a variable both DFO and base Data
Commons hold, then the one covering the most places or role tuples there,
then the most requested years, then the most observations, then the latest
observation, then a deterministic tie-break.

availability.description: where DFO holds observations of the variable; null, and named in gaps, when its read failed or the coverage index is not loaded

StatVarBlock.description: A variable's detail block: what it measures and where DFO holds observations of it.

Step.title: Step
Step.description:
One operation: its inputs by role, its one fixed policy, the caller's own choices,
what it kept, what data gaps it left out, the unit it produces, and, for an operation
that writes a new variable (sum, quotient, share, comparison), that variable's bare dcid in
`stat_var`.

A step takes either `input` or `inputs`, or neither, never both. `stat_var` is the bare
dcid of the variable a step that makes a new one (a sum, quotient, share or comparison)
writes its rows under. `sides` holds, by input role, each role column whose slice of that
input holds one entity, with that entity's ref. A comparison records it.

StepRef.title: StepRef
StepRef.description:
A reference: the dcid or id it names, and optionally the words for it.

`at_mint` marks a label taken from the evidence stored when the version was made.

TimeWindow.description: A date window. Absence of a bound means open-ended in that direction.

total.title: Total

Timing.title: Timing
Timing.description:
Latency breakdown, reused at two scopes: the envelope's own
diagnostics.timing_ms, where total is the whole request's wall-clock
elapsed time and by_step names the steps that run once per request,
shared across every part (coverage; extract; cache_lookup on a raw-text
request with the response cache active; entity_check on a request that
runs the place check), and a part's own timing_ms, where total sums
that part's own by_step values and by_step names the steps that part
ran plus a phase_<name> entry for each phase it ran, holding the time
no step booked, excluding the shared steps already reported on the
envelope. A part's shape_arcs, shape_probe, shape_probe_coverage,
shape_labels, shape_groups and shape_admission steps are nested inside
its shape step, so its total leaves them out.

recipe.description: the conversion recipe class that ran

TraceConversion.title: TraceConversion
TraceConversion.description:
A Spec-level record of a unit-conversion recipe. The engine converts
per series and records each converted series' recipe and tables in
ObservationSeries.conversion, since one Spec's series can convert under
different recipes. ResolutionTrace.conversion is modelled here but always
absent. Capabilities.recipe_classes lists the recipe members this
deployment applies.

removed_stat_vars.title: Removed Stat Vars

TraceDefaultReading.title: TraceDefaultReading
TraceDefaultReading.description:
The default price-basis reading applied before bind. Price bases rank Nominal,
RealValue, InflationAdjusted, then PurchasingPowerParity, with any basis the query names
moved first. A StatVar leaves the menu when a StatVar of a better-ranked basis with the
same constraints holds data wherever it does over the requested years. The trace records
whether the step ran and the StatVars it removed.

changes_magnitude.title: Changes Magnitude

UnitBlock.title: GraphUnitBlock
UnitBlock.description: A unit's detail block: the words `unit_words` names it by.

UnitConstantPricesRequestBinding.description:

currencies.description: each currency a unit request accepts that converts at least one served year at current prices, at a constant-price base year, or both, sorted by code

default_base_year.title: Default Base Year
default_base_year.description: the base year a constant-price request that names none completes to: the deflatorBaseYear every conversion table declares

role_currencies.description: the ISO 4217 code of the national currency (the graph's nationalCurrencyOf arc) of the one entity bound on each role, among `currencies`. UnitConversion.description:

that role. The role must be one the resolved StatVar declares.

UnitCurrentPricesRequestBinding.description:

no `base_year` member.

UnitsFold.description: A series' units: how many, the two covering the most places, and how many more.

code.title: Code
code.description: the reason, a code from the platform registry

pointer.title: Pointer
pointer.description: a JSON Pointer into `definition` (not the request body) naming the binding at fault -- a text-door request has no structured body to point into

cause.description: why this refusal fired, present only for code=recipe_not_declared (the structured door's same-named ProblemDetails extension); omitted on every other code

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: the canonical definition as interpreted -- {schema_version, identity: {identity_version, shape, slots, entities, facets, requested_window}} -- without spec_id, since this was never a resolvable construction

Unsupported.title: Unsupported
Unsupported.description:
The request was valid and fully understood, but not supported.

Fires for a text-door condition the request grammar or this deployment
cannot honour: the unit binder recognises but cannot represent a unit
phrase at all -- PPP terms, per-capita, a percent/share unit, or a scale
word (million/billion/thousand) -- code unit_request_unsupported, or a
recognised facet axis this deployment cannot bind (code
facet_binding_unsupported). A unit phrase the request form COULD
represent, but that this text failed to parse cleanly (two conflicting
currencies, price bases, or base years in one ask; an incomplete "base
year" cue with no year value), is a different outcome entirely: it lands
no_data with reason unit_not_resolved, never here. Distinct from every
refusal: the request was never malformed or unresolvable, so this is a
200, not a problem-details body.

variable_text.title: Variable Text
variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.

separate.title: Separate
separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. Two parts marked separate that resolve to one reading carry the same spec_id and stay two parts. False, the default, is omitted

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence
rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order, and a candidates part's then closes with its assumptions clause. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.

sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan
sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

entity_refs.title: Entity Refs
entity_refs.description: the binding of each entity of `restatement`, one per restatement.entities row, in row order, so a client can tell which node a text such as 'G7' bound. A response field kept off `restatement`, which posts back unchanged. The binding is the one the answer reads: for a candidates part, the elected reading's; for a part folded into an earlier part's spec, its own. [] when `restatement` is null or names no entity

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none

departures.title: Departures
departures.description: every way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, ordered by how much each changes the number: closest_match, measure_not_applied, operation_not_applied, breakdown_not_applied, entity_unavailable, year_unavailable, modelled_values, group_read_as_members, whole_total_read, whole_total_unpublished, direction_discarded, direction_inferred, scope_limited. [] when the answer is what was asked. A client that renders its own sentence reads them here; each one's text also closes the sentence that carries this part (see Departure.text). A warning on the same part reports run health and stays separate

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.description: every value the engine filled that the request did not ask for, in clause order. Declared defaults come first, in the order of the Spec's trace.slot_filters, then open roles, then the place scope. A declared default is a slot the request left open that its code system's or shape's declared default fixed, named by the bound code's full label. An open role is a flow role no request word asked for, read across every entity on it with data. It is either a role the role scope default filled (resolved.scope on that axis), whatever its member count, served as one series per member where the shape declares the role, or a role the heading states with no entity of its own ('from 164 providers', 'owed to all creditors'), served as the total over its members. A role the identity binds in entities or lists in open_roles, that one of the part's operations runs over ('top 5 donors'), or that the request's words asked every member of ('all donors'), is asked. The place scope is a request that named no place, read across every place with data. Every door fills assumptions. A definite part reads them from its Spec, a candidates part carries the items every list in CandidatesPart.reading_assumptions holds alike, text included, and no_data and unsupported parts carry []. A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts every slot bound, so its part states the items of the entry's assumptions echo that still hold (see ResubmitIdentityEntry.assumptions), and a candidates entry reads each reading with its candidate's echo (see ResubmitCandidate.assumptions). The sentence that carries this part closes with them as one segment='assumption' clause ('Assumed: official development assistance; every provider.'), after its departures. [] when the answer fills nothing

UnsupportedPart.title: UnsupportedPart
UnsupportedPart.description: This part's variable was valid and understood, but not supported.

measured_property.description: the measuredProperty; null when the variable declares none

stat_type.description: the statType; null when the variable declares none or its read failed

source_indicator_codes.title: Source Indicator Codes
source_indicator_codes.description: the sourceIndicatorCode arc's values: the codes naming the source series, as the publisher codes it (IMF WEO GDP carries NGDP and NGDPD); empty when it has none

definitions.title: Definitions

VariableDefinition.title: GraphVariableDefinition
VariableDefinition.description:
What a variable measures, part by part.

`constraints` are ordered by property dcid: the code index holds a variable's constraints
as a mapping with no declared order, and the graph's `constraintProperties` arc has none.

VariableSide.title: VariableSide
VariableSide.description:
One side of a composed unit that counts a variable in place of a unit, such as the
population in a per-capita denominator. `stat_var` is the variable's bare dcid.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: every change, group by group in order

VersionRef.title: VersionRef

A Datasets version: a `spec_` id with its `cv_` content version, or an `ops_` id with

spec_id.title: Spec Id
spec_id.description: the spec_id this warning attaches to, when it concerns one returned spec specifically; omitted otherwise

params.title: Params
params.description: the counts and labels the message states, for a client to compose its own text. observations_series_truncated: {shown, total, order}, the series shown, the confirmed series behind them, and how the shown series were chosen: 'ranked' (the most recent and largest) or 'fixed' (a selection made before values were read, not ranked by value). elected_shape_no_data: {no_data, elected}, the labels of the readings with no data and of the readings answered instead. un_system_unavailable: {places, variables, variable_labels}, the place dcids the UN front door refused, the variables of the UN reads that failed, each empty when none, and each variable's graph name, in variables order, '' where the graph holds none; a warning without params says the UN search itself was unavailable. whole_total_available: {total, total_label, whole_of}, the dcid and label of the total the source publishes for the side the answer lists member by member, and the classes of party it covers, comma-joined (official, private, residual). currency_unmapped_omitted: {count, entities, entity_labels}, how many entities the conversion left out, the dcids of the first ten, sorted, and each one's name, in entities order, '' where the conversion tables hold none, which is usual here, since an entity no currency names, such as a regional aggregate, is rarely in those tables; its dcid stays in entities. deflator_missing_omitted: the same with entity_years, the years each entity's rows were left out, as runs of consecutive years ('1990-2001, 2004'), in entities order; a warning without params says the loaded tables cannot tell which entities. Omitted for every other code

Warning.title: Warning
Warning.description:
A run-health signal. Note: this name shadows the Python builtin Warning.

Only `observations_series_truncated`, `elected_shape_no_data`, `un_system_unavailable`,
`whole_total_available`, `currency_unmapped_omitted` and `deflator_missing_omitted` set
`params`. A `None` `params` is left out of every dump, so other codes' warnings stay
exactly `{code, severity, message}` plus `spec_id` where one applies.

contributing_member_count.title: Contributing Member Count

stat_var_ref.title: Stat Var Ref

stat_var_label.title: Stat Var Label
stat_var_label.description: stat_vars_summed only: the family's label, the string the presentation door gives `stat_var_ref` on a chart (`code_index.labels.family_label` over the spec identity: its measure partition label, then its bound slots' labels); absent when neither has a label

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: coverage_below_scope only, when it names a group member: how many series the group requested

off_cadence_members.description: coverage_below_scope only: the group members holding observations in the requested years at another frequency than the group serves, which the figures leave out; absent when there are none

out_of_window_members.description: coverage_below_scope only: the group members holding no observation in the requested years; absent when there are none, and when the served provenance reads an absent member as zero

unserved_entities.description: coverage_below_scope only: the entities the request binds that served no observation, sorted; absent when there are none

requested_years.description: coverage_below_scope only: the year range the request asked for, when the data covers fewer of its years; absent otherwise

served_years.description: coverage_below_scope only: the years the data covers, both bounds set, beside requested_years; absent otherwise

omitted_entities.description: currency_unmapped_omitted only: the entities whose rows the conversion left out, sorted

omitted_entity_years.description: deflator_missing_omitted only: the entities whose rows the conversion left out for a missing deflator, sorted, each with the years of those rows

WarningModel.title: WarningModel
WarningModel.description:
One manifest warning. Only `stat_vars_summed` sets its three structured fields, a
group's `coverage_below_scope` its three member fields, `coverage_below_scope`
`unserved_entities`, `requested_years` and `served_years`, `currency_unmapped_omitted`
`omitted_entities`, and
`deflator_missing_omitted` `omitted_entity_years`. A `None` field is left out of every dump, so other codes' warnings, on
the wire and in stored version bodies, stay exactly `{code, severity, message}`.

enrichment_fields.title: Enrichment Fields
enrichment_fields.description: enrichment field names this deployment enables. A live token qualifies one as {entity_column}_{field} on the columns option. Three fields come from the code index's declaration of a party: party_kind is its kind (party, total, residual); party_class is official, private or residual, and for a total the one class its whole markers cover, empty when they cover none or several; party_whole is true on a row whose party is a total that holds every party of its classes on its axis in that row's dataset and year, such as Official Donors, Total, false on a row where it is not, and empty where the row names no one dataset and year, as in a pivot. A bare party field token requests it for every role on a flow axis the table has, and a file holds a party field only when a token asks for it. Long output writes one {role}_kind beside {role}_label for every role on a flow axis instead, in words: official or private for a provider or creditor, country or organisation for a recipient or debtor, total, whole total or unallocated, and ignores party field tokens. A party field qualifies no subject role, so observationAbout_party_kind refuses column_unknown. A party the index does not list gets an empty cell and an enrichment_unavailable warning

decode_code_systems.title: Decode Code Systems
decode_code_systems.description: code systems the packaged code index declares, sorted. Decoding is always on when a rendered frame's StatVars declare one of these -- there is no opt-out. Long output writes each as a {code_system} column (the StatVar's code in that system) and a {code_system}_label column (its label); pivot output, frame-layout output (layout: "frame"), groupby.by and the columns option name it stat_var_{code_system}, the label column

default_facet_policies_live.title: Default Facet Policies Live
default_facet_policies_live.description: whether the graph declares its own per-StatVar/per-source default facet policy; false does not mean an unbound axis refuses -- see default_facet_policy

default_facet_policy.description: this deployment's own default-facet policy, consulted for an unbound axis once the graph declares none; null if this deployment enforces no fallback of its own

summability_declarations_live.title: Summability Declarations Live
summability_declarations_live.description: whether the graph declares its own per-axis summability; true unconditionally, the same way decode carries no separate liveness gate

summable_axes.title: Summable Axes
summable_axes.description: code systems the packaged code index declares summable, sorted -- the axes a groupby request may name in `by` to keep, with every other declared-summable axis this frame decoded collapsed into it

groupby_level_axes.title: Groupby Level Axes
groupby_level_axes.description: code systems the packaged code index declares summable, hierarchical, and disjoint from children (a parent-coded record excludes its children's), sorted. These are the axes groupby.levels accepts, each rolled up to one depth of its parent chain (0 = root codes) before the sum

definition_candidate_cap.title: Definition Candidate Cap
definition_candidate_cap.description: the reverse-arc page a described-arm definition's member walk reads first; a page that fills it without a confirmed root sends the walk to the whole filtered set, up to definition_subject_ceiling

definition_subject_ceiling.title: Definition Subject Ceiling
definition_subject_ceiling.description: ceiling on the whole filtered reverse-arc set a described-arm definition's member walk reads when its first page cannot settle the family; a larger set refuses over_ceiling (candidate_window), and a walk past its read deadline answers timeout (504, retryable)

sync_budget_rows.title: Sync Budget Rows
sync_budget_rows.description: sync budget: a mint/definition request whose own coverage estimate (series_coverage.index.CoverageIndex.estimate) stays at or under this many rows, and at or under sync_budget_requests SDMX requests, runs inline

sync_budget_requests.title: Sync Budget Requests
sync_budget_requests.description: the SDMX request half of the sync budget -- see sync_budget_rows

async_max_rows.title: Async Max Rows
async_max_rows.description: async ceiling: an over-sync-budget mint/definition request whose own coverage estimate (series_coverage.index.CoverageIndex.estimate) stays at or under this many rows, and at or under async_max_requests SDMX requests, is recorded as an operation and answered 202; over either, it is refused over_ceiling (ceiling_kind operation_rows) before any operation is recorded

async_max_requests.title: Async Max Requests
async_max_requests.description: the SDMX request half of the async ceiling -- see async_max_rows; crossing this one alone refuses over_ceiling with ceiling_kind operation_requests

pivot_max_output_cells.title: Pivot Max Output Cells
pivot_max_output_cells.description: cap on a pivot's total output cell count (rows x columns) before pivot_over_cell_cap

operation_retention_days.title: Operation Retention Days
operation_retention_days.description: how long a terminal (done/failed) operation stays guaranteed pollable (contract, 'The operation envelope'). A done operation's own manifest is guaranteed servable for exactly this long, since it is bounded by the same working-tier artifact clock every other mint/definition response is (dataset_store.snapshot.WORKING_TIER_RETENTION) -- pinning it extends that the same way pinning any other snapshot does. A daily maintenance job deletes done and failed operations last updated more than this many days ago, so a poll after that answers operation_not_found

graph_api__resolve_models__ResolveReques.title: GraphResolveRequest
graph_api__resolve_models__ResolveReques.description:
`texts`: 1 to 25 strings resolved as one batch. Each is stripped of surrounding
whitespace and must then be 1 to 200 characters.

`kinds` admits only candidates of those kinds. It defaults to `DEFAULT_RESOLVE_KINDS`, so a
request that omits it equals one naming those eight. `code` searches the code index's labels
and synonyms, and `code_system` narrows codes to one system's graph id

`/code_system`. `expand: ["members"]` inlines a group's or region's members.

ProblemDetails.description:
RFC 9457 problem-details body for every non-2xx response.

Standard base fields (type, title, status, detail) plus the platform
registry's stable extensions (code, pointer, alternatives, truncated,
issues, constraint_id, trace_id, capability_version, retryable). Optional
members (pointer, alternatives, truncated, issues, constraint_id) are
omitted from the wire body when absent -- callers should serialize with
``model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)``, which ``to_json`` does.

type.description: a relative URI reference to the code's registry entry
type.title: Type

title.description: short, human-readable summary of the problem type
title.title: Title

code.description: the stable machine-readable code from the platform registry
code.title: Code

pointer.title: Pointer

alternatives.description: values that would satisfy this request, when known

truncated.title: Truncated

constraint_id.description: the machine-keyable id of the constraint this refusal violates, when known
constraint_id.title: Constraint Id

ceiling_kind.description: for over_ceiling: which ceiling was crossed -- member_cardinality, candidate_window, rows, or bytes
ceiling_kind.title: Ceiling Kind

count.description: for over_ceiling: the observed count, in ceiling_kind's own unit, that crossed cap -- omitted only when the count itself is unmeasured, never when it is merely large. Under candidate_window it is the candidates the read actually returned, at most cap: a read that fills its window returns exactly cap, and one that stops early on a surviving continuation token returns fewer
count.title: Count

cap.description: for over_ceiling: the ceiling, in ceiling_kind's own unit, that count crossed. Under candidate_window it is the candidate window the read was allowed
cap.title: Cap

trace_id.description: this request's trace_id, shared with diagnostics and the SSE done event
trace_id.title: Trace Id

retryable.title: Retryable

ProblemIssue.description:
One failure among several a single refusal can report at once.

Each issue carries its own pointer, the member or axis it concerns, its
own alternatives and truncation flag, and the machine code and message of
the failure it stands for -- mirroring the same-named top-level
ProblemDetails fields, but scoped to one entry among many.
Fields default to None and are omitted from the wire body when absent
(the envelope's omit-when-absent rule).
